tracks.description: Full orchestra plus piano. This is a long piece with several dynamic changes. Semi-heroic at times.

tracks.title: Noise Attack
tracks.description: Dark driving rock thing. Heavy on the drums... actually, heavy on the everything.

tracks.title: Nonstop
tracks.description: From what I can tell, this piece has no genre... it is an odd mix of a few things, but not enough of any one of them to be considered a member of that group. So, when you find a new critter which is certainly a new species... likely a new genus... probably a new family... and seriously might be a order. It has an exoskeleton, gives birth to live young (asexually somehow?), has a beak... We recognize all those parts, but it doesn't fit anything. Might be a new phylum.

tracks.title: Northern Glade
tracks.description: Are you sick of "high pressure" games that "keep score"? Yeah, me too. But I FIXED it! I made a game where literally nothing happens, and nothing matters! I enjoy playing as a chicken, though it grants you no special powers. I'm not sure what chicken powers would be. Brief and ponderous flight? Speak to other chickens? Super fast egg warming? You can experience “Northern Glade” here: https://incompetech.com/games/Magic%20Scout/

tracks.title: Not As It Seems
tracks.description: A quizzical harp and bell introduction transports you to a mysterious land of magic as bouncing horns and pounding bass drums signify peril. In the last twenty seconds an orchestra takes over and the intensity rises, leaving the scene in danger?s hands.

tracks.title: Notanico Merengue
tracks.instruments: Kit, Bass, Electric Guitar, Percussion, Trumpet, Bari Sax, Tenor Sax, Alto Sax, Piano
tracks.description: A floor thumping modern take on the meringue. Horns, guitar, piano, and a pile of percussion.

tracks.title: Nothing Broken
tracks.instruments: Clarinets, Flute, Harpsichord, Guitar, Organ, Kit
tracks.description: An uplifting very happy happy piece.  Clarinets and flutes open.  Main piece begins at 00:20.  Great for happy situations.

tracks.title: Nouvelle Noel
tracks.instruments: Guitar, Bass, Drums, Bells, Piano, Vibes
tracks.description: I say! It is such a lovely brisk day! Aren't the horses lovely? I mean... look at all the horseness they have! They are scoring quite high on the horse-o-meters today! Nothing bovine on this street, Nay! ... ... ... Wait... I was trying to make a joke involving a horse's "neigh" combined with the archaic positive/negative usage of "nay". Then everything went wrong, and I said almost the opposite of the intention. So, without the joke: Picture a street where the only animals are the horsiest of horses... No cows or pigs. Okay, there are two dogs... but one of them is pretty small... and you can see a cat in one of the windows... but MOSTLY horses. If you added up the weights of all the non-horse, non-humans in the picture, they would weigh less than one horse.

tracks.title: Nowhere Land
tracks.description: Fun fact: Working title was "Arpeggiator Rock From the 80s 1". Fun fact: This piece consist entirely of single notes being passed to a stack 5 different synths at the same time. Each synth has a different program running on it that triggers more notes. Fun fact: Scotland isn't a nation. It is technically an empire that claims sovereignty over Paraguay's 400k sheep and also Neptune's "shepherd" moon Despina.

tracks.title: Nu Flute
tracks.description: Eastern flute-like reed-like instrument - the Dizi.

tracks.title: Numinous Shine
tracks.description: Non-threatening light synths moving slowly.

tracks.title: Obliteration
tracks.instruments: Cellos, Basses, Organ, Violins, Violas, French Horns, Percussion
tracks.description: High-energy, fast-paced, and memorable, this is a great background to your 2D platformer. It was actually written for a 2D platformer, which is why it will loop back on itself so well. Like Ouroboros! If you're looking for a high school mascot, PLEASE consider Ouroboros. I'm not sure if it would make for great cheerleading routines, or if it would end up looking more like a human centipede.... But there is one way to fine out! Go! Fighting Ouroboroses!!

tracks.title: OctoBlues
tracks.description: Just yer basic 12-bar blues. Guitar courtesy Brett Van Donsel.

tracks.title: Odyssey
tracks.description: Regular electronic simple piece with a mix of straight and swing. Perfect for looping in space! Or maybe at the end of the world.

tracks.title: Off to Osaka
tracks.instruments: Kit, Bass, Piano, Trumpet, Tenor Sax, Vibe
tracks.description: Super bouncy be-bop jazz. Crazy vibe solo.

tracks.title: Oh, Christmas Tree
tracks.description: Slightly jazzy quick sing-along.

tracks.title: Oh, Little Town of Bethlehem
tracks.description: Texturally thick in parts.

tracks.title: Old Road
tracks.description: This music is the introduction to your characters entering a Middle Eastern village for the first time. The tribal drumming is all hustle and bustle, while the melody is winding, forceful, and unfamiliar.

tracks.title: Olde Timey
tracks.description: Background ragtime feel that won't attract attention to itself.

tracks.title: Ominous
tracks.description: Uneven foreboding short cue, winds play opposite strings.

tracks.title: Ominous Intro
tracks.description: Slow moving, and moog-like.

tracks.title: On Hold for You
tracks.description: The tenor sax performance in this piece was done by an AI musician. The notes and chords were generated algorithmically (not by an AI). https://sites.research.google/tonetransfer  0:33 there is an amazingly smooth and correct sounding run-up.  0:50 it goes below the actual tenor sax range. I love how it extrapolated down there! 0:58 there's some leak hiss going on at 0:58. I'll call that "artistic license". 1:08 it goes quite a bit above the standard range for a tenor sax, but those notes should be available in altissimo with some fancy fingerings. 2:20 you can almost taste the spit! 2:58 it plays the same note back to back, but changes the tone of the note. Very cool.  This ToneTransfer AI Sax is amazing. Getting this level of detail in a recording with standard virtual instruments is almost impossible. AI for the win!

tracks.title: On My Way
tracks.instruments: Bass, Guitar, Flutes, Clarinets, Vibes, Drums
tracks.description: If you're not adding to the narrative; get out of the way! This piece gets out of the way... You can put it under any monolog, dialog, timelapse... actually, with a timelapse, you could probably find something a little more interesting with some pacing, or something. So... this is for those sure nice videos. Guaranteed* to offend as few people as possible!  *"Guaranteed" is used in this context for entertainment purposes only.

tracks.title: On the Cool Side
tracks.instruments: Bass, Kit, Trumpet, Tenor Sax, EP
tracks.description: Very cool.

tracks.title: On the Ground
tracks.description: A cool sort of background cop beat track.

tracks.title: On the Passing of Time
tracks.description: A slow somber piano piece. Small amount of reverb to the notes.  Ends early, last 20 seconds dedicated to a fadeout.

tracks.title: On the Shore
tracks.description: Beautiful, thoughtful piece worthy of character reflection.

tracks.title: One of Them
tracks.description: Calm opening with giant hit around 1:50 that calms down some and ends on grating tones.

tracks.title: One Sly Move
tracks.description: A slow, relaxed, electronic piece.  This piece heavily uses EP and Synths.  From 1:01 to 1:20 all goes silent except the EP.  Mainly a synth and EP piece, guitar and kit in the background.

tracks.title: One-eyed Maestro
tracks.instruments: Accordion, Violin, Percussion, Flutes, Trumpets, Horns, Strings
tracks.description: This is the kind of music that makes skeletons dance. With its pounding brass, singsong flute melody, and off-kilter syncopation, this piece is whimsical and reminiscent of a carnival. It is quirky, quick, playful, and dangerously creepy, and is perfect for a lively cartoon, circus-themed content, or a magician?s show.

tracks.title: Onion Capers
tracks.description: Hey buddy, that is quite the sack of onions you have! If I had a sack of onions like that, I'd be happier than a tree on Arbor Day! Everyone wants to get their hand in an onion sack like that.  Me? I like a nice purple onion, but you don't get to pick favorites when you got your hand in an onion sack. A big yellow one can feel like a little purple one. You won't know 'til you pull it out, and by then you already got yourself an onion. I know most folks don't want strangers mucking about in unfamiliar onion sacks these days, so I'll be on my way. But, that is quite the sack of onions you have.  To perform the monolog "Onion Capers" at your school or event, speak the words out loud at your school or event.

tracks.title: Open Those Bright Eyes
tracks.description: This piece is made up of three distinct variations on a melodic theme, and should be taken apart and used for transitions in a light-hearted short video. The first section begins with a bright, leading to the big push of the bombastic brass. The second section, beginning at 0:52, is the same melody, but only features the piano. This section is softer and lasts 20 seconds. The final section begins at 1:17, and ends with an excited flourish.

tracks.title: Opium
tracks.description: Slow, dreamy, droning piece that has a trance-inducing effect.

tracks.title: Opportunity Walks
tracks.description: Up-tempo 2-piano combo (with bass and drums). Dark in the choruses - lighter in the middle sections.

tracks.title: Oppressive Gloom
tracks.feel: Dark, Eerie, Epic, Mysterious, Somber, Suspenseful
tracks.description: Moody moody dark score. Almost a death march. Loops pretty darned well - but you need to trim the end.

tracks.title: Organic Grunge
tracks.description: A sort of funky, rocking, semi-swinging piece with enough dirt to make it cool. Like... jeans that were previously worn by coal miners that are sold in high-end stores.

tracks.title: Organic Meditations One
tracks.description: Very long, very calming piece in D Flat major. Part one of a series of three.

tracks.title: Organic Meditations Three
tracks.description: Very long, very calming piece in D Flat major. Part two of a series of three.

tracks.title: Organic Meditations Two
tracks.description: Very long, very calming piece in D Flat major. Part two of a series of three.

tracks.title: Orion 300XB
tracks.description: Unintelligible alien transmissions punctuate the entirety of this piece, while simple, distracted chords create an atmosphere of unease and wonder -  beauty and discovery. The pace is quick, and the taiko drumming is foreboding and tribal, but the airy beauty of the chords is almost calming.

tracks.title: Ossuary 1 - A Beginning
tracks.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary". This piece is a slow-moving edgy drone with an ethereal melody on top. Since this is sort of a new genre, I'm not exactly sure where it is appropriate. Maybe a vampire spa? Dinner music for a psychopath? You'll figure it out!

tracks.title: Ossuary 2 - Turn
tracks.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 2: Turn More aggressive than part one, something is most certainly going down here. Perfect for; seeing how far down the rabbit hole goes, Loch Ness expeditions, videos about giant capacitors, dinner parties where you want everyone uncomfortable. Gets quite awful around the 3:15 mark. Awful in a good way.

tracks.title: Ossuary 3 - Words
tracks.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 3: Words Odd metals and percussion underscore the only piece in the series with a clear clean synth. There's some amount of technology under this thing. The synth is quickly overtaken by the bizarre drones. Perfect for; being stranded in space... in a ship.

tracks.title: Ossuary 4 - Animate
tracks.description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 4: Animate It is coming for us!!!! ARGH!!!!! RUN! But where!?? Doesn't matter! Try running at the walls!!! No good! They're solid!! Is it still coming!? ARGH! Yup! There it is!!!! Now where!? The ladder!? NO GOOD COMES FROM CLIMBING A LADDER! You should know that by now! It'll just break halfway up OR something will grab your ankle OR BOTH! Just save yourself! There's no good us both getting eaten by that thing!!! Oh! And when you fill out the survey - this holiday was "VERY DISAPPOINTING!"

tracks.title: Ossuary 5 - Rest
tracks.description: After some amount of introspection, I can only conclude that this is the afterlife, or some entryway to the afterlife... or a really cool club in the Meatpacking district after-hours. This is the most genuinely relaxing piece of the Ossuary suite... still has a bit of an edge.

tracks.title: Ossuary 6 - Air
tracks.description: Well, something has taken a turn for the not-quite-as-good-as-I'd-like. Slow-moving drone of impending doom!

tracks.title: Ossuary 7 - Resolve
tracks.description: Well, we've come to some sort of ending here... Our relaxation journey is complete, but to be honest, I've had more relaxing times clinging to the single floating piece of flotsam that resurfaced after the ship exploded.

tracks.title: Our Story Begins
tracks.description: Interesting 3/4 feel with an accelerando near the end. 5-note groupings pass from the winds to the strings for a while, and the winds come back at the end in a nifty way.

tracks.title: Ouroboros
tracks.description: Thick and simple electronic piece that sits somewhere between the late 1980s and 2014. Loopable.

tracks.title: Outfoxing the Fox
tracks.instruments: Synths, Percussion, Bass, Strings, Cellos, Violas, Violins
tracks.description: You threw a golf ball at me. But I saw that coming, so I had a tennis racquet handy. Then you threw a running chainsaw at me. But I saw it coming, so I had a plexiglass safety cage handy. I see that rabid ferret behind your back... I’ll be in the car.

tracks.title: Over Under
tracks.description: Solo bass. Non-consistant tempos. No looping, just playing.

tracks.title: Overcast
tracks.instruments: Bass, Kit, Synth, Guitar, Piano, Percussion
tracks.description: A dreamy, watery disco beat with a kick and snare that are slightly outside of classic disco. It seems like this might clear the dance floor at 3am.

tracks.title: Overheat
tracks.description: A slow, trance-inducing piece of minimalism with a touch of melody in parts.

tracks.title: Overriding Concern
tracks.feel: Driving, Action, Unnerving, Dark, Mysterious, Suspenseful
tracks.description: Slow fade in with source recordings from a carnival, leading to a clean sharp synth and round synth. Tubular bells and glock add interest later.

tracks.title: Overture
tracks.description: Opening theme I wrote for Nosferatu. Striking chord structure. Sweet melody.

tracks.title: Overworld
tracks.description: You want adventure? You want a princess? You're not getting the princess, buddy... but Adventure Awaits in "Overworld"! How much adventure? A statistically significant amount. Somewhere in the neighborhood of 18ppm... (or roughly 18 milligrams per liter... the density of adventure is unusually high, and in some cases even at 18ppm you will get a weight closer to 19mg/L.) Download comes with a faster version, a SUPER faster version, and a slower version without percussion for lazy title screens and whatnot.

tracks.title: Padanaya Blokov
tracks.description: Catchy Russian-sounding piece.

tracks.title: Pale Rider
tracks.description: Yes. A solo harp piece with an old western edge. I'm not sure why this hasn't been done before. Probably because you don't imagine a cowboy riding with a harp slung over his horse. It works, though.

tracks.title: Pamgaea
tracks.description: Super easy-going background made with sharp synths contrasted by washy synths.

tracks.title: Paradise Found
tracks.description: This piece of music never stops smiling. It is a happy, dancy, and never over-the-top party opener! The bass will move people. I found the "Tropical House" genre on some AI music site, and put this together. Overall, I'm a fan!

tracks.title: Parisian
tracks.description: Simple solo accordion piece in c minor. I did this to try out stereo accordion recording. Seems to work ok.

tracks.title: Parting of the Ways - Part 1
tracks.description: Impromptu in C Major. Development takes its time.

tracks.title: Parting of the Ways - Part 2
tracks.description: Impromptu in A Minor. Extreme dynamics may make this piece challenging to incorporate into projects.

tracks.title: Passing Action
tracks.description: This short piece is the accompaniment for the hero surreptitiously breaking into a corporation or headquarters. The reverberating congas, triangle, and synthesized percussion enhance the senses, while the bass guitar provides a strong groove. The strings raise in pitch, evoking a sense of building tension. High-pitched crescendo of strings at 0:45 is the climax of the suspense.

tracks.title: Past Sadness
tracks.description: We all need sadness sometimes. I have a sadness Loot-Box subscription. This month, I got some get-well cards for babies, wilted iceberg lettuce, a 1999 Gateway laptop, 3 popped balloons, and a die-hard Montreal Expos fan. The service ships everything in an empty box of wine with a broken spigot.

tracks.title: Past the Edge
tracks.description: Slow dark and empty with a solo voice.

tracks.title: Peace of Mind
tracks.description: Very calm, very long piece. Piano over a drone in D.

tracks.title: Peaceful Desolation
tracks.instruments: Brass, Tympani, Glock, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Strings
tracks.description: Low-key mood establisher with chords moving in parallel blocks for the melody. Starts dark, ends open and airy.

tracks.title: Pennsylvania Rose
tracks.description: Western-sounding piece written as an overture to a theatrical play. (themes stolen from an older piece of mine)

tracks.title: Pensif
tracks.description: Slow moving cluster chords. Beautiful, I say!

tracks.title: Penumbra
tracks.description: There is something in the shadows, it isn't quite perceptible, but you know it is there. This is designed to make people uneasy.

tracks.title: Pepper's Theme
tracks.description: Beautiful interplay between the piano and guitar, ending very upbeat. This was composed for the film "Duel" (2014).

tracks.title: Peppy Pepe
tracks.description: Hideously happy Latin piece. Nice trombone solo. Lots of auxiliary percussion.

tracks.title: Perigrine Grandeur
tracks.description: High energy distorted stringed instruments float above a tribal-type beat.

tracks.title: Perspectives
tracks.description: An interesting little piece with very organic synths and an occasional melodic flute.

tracks.title: Petulant March
tracks.description: Fun little impromptu in one take with lots of odd delay effects that give it a more lush feel.

tracks.title: Phantasm
tracks.instruments: Bells, Dulcimer, Synth, English Horn, Percussion, Flute
tracks.description: This piece stars a super-low bass line that physically unnerves. The bells and other melodies offer enough complexity to offset the simple repetitive lines.

tracks.title: Phantom from Space
tracks.description: I need to be careful about naming these things. Could be neo-retro sci-fi - could be straight up paranormal! Whatever it is, there is a major mystery to be had here! Ideal for technology-induced mummy reanimation films. The alternate mixes in the full download both give a slightly different feel - one with no percussion, and one without the theremin-like synth lead.

tracks.title: Phat Sketch
tracks.description: Sizzling fat analog bass line with a little beat.

tracks.title: Piano Between
tracks.description: Just a light piano piece for linking scenes.

tracks.title: Piece for Disaffected Piano One
tracks.description: I hesitate to assign a 'feel' to this because it is so exotic. It uses a 19 semitone scale which does not repeat at the octave. There are 9 semitones to a perfect fifth. The tuning is Wendy Carlos' "Alpha" scale. The piano strings are laid to horrible pain in sections as two octaves of keyboard are used to represent a doubling of frequency.

tracks.title: Piece for Disaffected Piano Two
tracks.description: Like "PfDP One", this piece also uses the Alpha scale developed by Wendy Carlos. Improvising on this piano is like walking in a minefield. There are many places to step which are just fine, but every now and again you find a surprise. This piece is light, and even comical in parts - with some musical revelations in between.

tracks.title: Pilot Error
tracks.description: Rock music without a bass guitar? Yeah, the piano carries that line.

tracks.title: Pinball Spring
tracks.description: Triumphant and exuberant, this arcade groove is bright and perfect for retro games or humorous video content. It has a thumping beat that is light-hearted, and is easily looped for continuous play.

tracks.title: Pinball Spring 160
tracks.description: Triumphant and exuberant, this arcade groove is bright and perfect for retro games or humorous video content. Super fast J-Pop feel version.

tracks.title: Pippin the Hunchback
tracks.description: Understated medieval-type piece. Loopable.

tracks.title: Pixel Peeker Polka - faster
tracks.description: 8-bit-sounding electronic polka.

tracks.title: Pixel Peeker Polka - slower
tracks.description: 8-bit sounding electronic polka.  8-bit-sounding electronic polka.

tracks.title: Pixelland
tracks.description: What do you get when you cross some 8-bit music technology with Dixieland music? Well... you get stuff that sounds like this. The uncompressed download comes with a pile of extra stuff, like versions at 220, 230, 240, and a whopping 275 beats per minute! That's really fast. It also has loops that don't go through the modulation so you can repeat them as long as you'd like!

tracks.title: Plain Loafer
tracks.description: Sort of rock, but not. Neither is this jazz or funk... I really don't know what this is... but it is kind of fun.

tracks.title: Plaint
tracks.description: Slow moving piece for bassoon (very high on the instrument) and harp. Works very well behind dialog, and gives a sense of grief.

tracks.title: Pleasant Porridge
tracks.description: Attention in the lobby: The show will begin shortly. Please find your seat.  Souvenir programs are available for purchase at every entrance. Remember to set your bleeping devices to non-bleepie mode. This show features flashing lights, live bats, and almond butter.  If you have a condition  that may cause problems, please see us at the ticket counter for further information. The show will begin shortly!

tracks.title: Plucky Daisy
tracks.description: Unsteady quaint day-in-the-park type theme.

tracks.title: Political Action Ad
tracks.description: Background to an evil political action ad. Add your own alarmist voice over - this was engineered to make people uncomfortable, and not interfere with human voice range. "Tell your congressman to vote NO on the Pollute Our Drinking Water and Send All of Our Money to Canada Act."

tracks.title: Poofy Reel
tracks.description: Funtastic little piece written for a movie trailer's more quirky section.

tracks.title: Pookatori and Friends
tracks.description: Are your eyeballs soft? Let's be delightful with Pookatori! It is extremely happy to drink when you are thirsty. Pookatori will help! Pookatori always helps! Are you aware of your own defect? Pookatori will smile to your grandmother every day! Would you like a beautiful pie? Pookatori has many friends made from a magic and people balls. Let's have fun with Pookatori's friends! Do you like to absorbing? Functional!!

tracks.title: Pop Goes the Weasel
tracks.description: Heavy bass drums and an string bass set the tone for this dark and menacing tone. The familiar refrain then plays, but is made expressive and almost violent as it is played on several string basses and cellos. The pace is rather quick and forceful, and after the quick ending, a jack-in-the-box plays, normally child-like, but made creepy because of the sinister music that came before.

tracks.title: Poppers and Prosecco
tracks.description: What's the difference between a dead frog in the road, and a dead trombone player in the road? The frog was probably going to a gig! Hah! Get it? Well... it took me 8 years to get it, so let me explain. When you go out hunting frogs, that is called "gigging". Gigging is bad for a frog. When you go out playing an instrument in a band for money, that is called "gigging". Gigging is good for a trombone player... but man, you gotta be good. You pretty much need a bass player and a drummer... not many people need a trombone player, so they typically don't get many gigs... Did I explain that right? Wait, let me start over...

tracks.title: Porch Blues
tracks.description: Guitar, harmonica, piano 12 bar blues in D.

tracks.title: Porch Swing Days - faster
tracks.description: Acoustic guitars play a constantly flowing feel-good melody, enhanced by an airy chorus that enters early in the piece. The music is bright and evokes a carefree attitude towards life and the troubles of the world.

tracks.title: Porch Swing Days - slower
tracks.description: Acoustic guitars play a constantly flowing feel-good melody, enhanced by an airy chorus that enters early in the piece. The music is bright and evokes a carefree attitude towards life and the troubles of the world.

tracks.title: Port Horizon
tracks.instruments: Drums, Bass, Vibraphone, Guitar, Trumpet, Trombones, Violins, Other
tracks.description: Welcome to the tropical paradise of Port Horizon. Not much to do here but listen to the short wave radios and play guitar. There is also food and drinks with those little umbrellas... Other than that - not much. Except snorkeling. Snorkeling is pretty cool. Oh, there is also Art Night on Tuesday - where you get a volleyball and some paints and make yourself a friend! Beach chess... I forgot about Beach Chess. Don't play white against Todd, though - he plays all-Hedgehog all the time. Come on, Todd - just once, seriously ONCE could you play King's Indian or... you know what? I'd even take the French Defence; Exchange Variation, you boring symmetrical jerk.

tracks.title: Power Restored
tracks.description: Turbulent low brass and snare countered by high winds. High energy.

tracks.title: Prelude and Action
tracks.description: Building piece that sets up some sweet, sweet action.

tracks.title: Prelude in C (BWV 846)
tracks.description: J. S. Bach. This is the famous first piece of the Well Tempered Clavier, Book 1. Performed on piano. Very clean recording.

tracks.title: Presenterator
tracks.description: 90s vintage presentation music with a bit more production value than the buy-out music of the day.

tracks.title: Private Eye
tracks.description: Styled in the bluesy swing of a 70?s cop drama TV show, Private Eye incorporates slick rhythms with a prominent bass line and competing bursts of horns. The final thirty seconds builds in volume with the congas until the abrupt finish.

tracks.title: Private Reflection
tracks.feel: Dark, Eerie, Epic, Intense, Somber, Unnerving
tracks.description: Epic myth. Part of the hero's journey. Starts with a solo soprano, and later mixes a full choir. Ends assuming you'll mix it into another piece.

tracks.title: Procession of the King
tracks.description: A strings only piece, evocative of love, romance, and pride. Just before the one minute mark the music takes an unexpected turn, becoming intensely emotional and beautiful as the strings play in the higher register with a slight tremolo, with the bass filling up the empty space in the last half minute.

tracks.title: Professor and the Plant
tracks.instruments: Small Ensemble - Harp, Bassoon, Trumpet, Glock
tracks.description: Two short pieces in one file. Deliberate clockwork theme.

tracks.title: Professor Umlaut
tracks.description: This piece started its life as a random challenge on a show I do on Twitch.tv called "The Wheels of Doom!". The 4 randomized elements that came together here were: Drum Machine, Strings, Xylophone, and Comedic. I think it worked out pretty well!

tracks.title: Promises to Keep
tracks.description: Slow impromptu for solo piano. A little hopeful, a little sorrowful... I'm sure there is a word for this feeling, but I don't know it.

tracks.title: Promising Relationship
tracks.description: A striking chordal change keeps the first and second halves different.

tracks.title: Protofunk
tracks.description: Lots of guitar effects built over a clean beat. Dan Ritter on guitar.

tracks.title: Psychedelic Crater
tracks.instruments: Sitar synth, electronic drums and bass
tracks.description: Harsh yet simple piece. The main theme was played with a wiimote, so don't expect too much expression! Extra interest kicks in at 1:35.

tracks.title: Pulse
tracks.description: Nice groove in this one. Highly chorused guitar overlay.

tracks.title: Pump
tracks.description: Longer version of the fast-paced rockin' tune from the fictional band Glory Nugget. Oh yeah, it is bad, and that's what makes it great.

tracks.title: Pure Attitude
tracks.description: A bouncy electronica piece heavily featuring strings and synths.

tracks.title: Pyro Flow
tracks.description: You got flow? You want this. Borderline chill and aggressive, this piece is your man! It does stand alone, but if you got words... it is amazing! Try it! What style is this? I'm not sure. It borrows from a lot - but I don't think it fits anything out there. Rickenbacker bass, gnarled piano, and a distorted drum kit all fit together beautifully. Percussion breakdown at 2:17.

tracks.title: Quasi Motion
tracks.description: I don't know what genre this is. Sort of Latin? Broadly? So, if you're looking for something unlike anything else... this may be it.

tracks.title: Quiet Panic
tracks.description: Quiet tremolo strings that build slightly to an anti-climax.

tracks.title: Quinn's Song:  A New Man
tracks.description: This piece starts with piano, and ends with tymp. It uses a reharmonized theme taken from Chopin. One of 3 pieces with this theme.

tracks.title: Quinn's Song: First Night
tracks.description: This piece contains 2 themes, one in 7/4 time, and another borrowed from Chopin - and set among very disturbing chords.

tracks.title: Quinn's Song: The Dance Begins
tracks.description: This piece takes its main theme from Chopin, completely reharmonizes it, and gives it a different setting. One of three pieces with this theme.

tracks.title: Quirky Dog
tracks.description: Smooth and jazzy ditty with a fun edge for all your light humor needs! Okay, many of your light humor needs. Excellent for montage sequences dealing with bureaucracy.

tracks.title: Radio Martini
tracks.instruments: Guitar, Kit, Bass, Clarinet, Flute, Bass Clarinet, Violas
tracks.description: Prominent clarinet means this is a bad tune to have under dialog, but with no dialog - it is quite neat.

tracks.title: Rainbows
tracks.description: Light and refreshing as a summer's day! I really just should lift ad copy for laundry detergent and fabric softener for this one. Springtime Fresh Scent! Pure and Simple! Brightens! Gentle on Fabrics! Great Value! Easy-pour Bottle! Marimbas!

tracks.title: Rains Will Fall
tracks.description: Slow Waltz. English Waltz. Foxtrot. Slow Fox. The piano plays a mournful, waltzing melody, while strings enter gently. Halfway into the second minute, the tone is more hopeful, but then returns to the sadness of the introduction.  Just before the third minute ends the hope returns, but melts again into sadness with the final high note of the piano. This is music for a rainy day, or when the hero to a story has lost his way.

tracks.title: Ranz des Vaches
tracks.description: Ranz des Vaches or "Call to the Dairy Cows" is a small but famous section of the overture to William Tell by Rossini. It is most often used to depict morning or sleepiness in cartoons. Hook starts at 0:21.

tracks.title: Raving Energy
tracks.description: There's always someone who is uncomfortably excited. This is for all you border collies hopped up on Adderall. This music is dangerously energetic and may cause paranoia, anxiety, and/or hallucinations.  Not the fun kind of hallucinations, either. These are the kind of hallucinations where ponies with 8 spider-like legs are climbing on your ceiling and walls while singing "Barbie Girl" and criticizing your overly-bland dating profile.

tracks.title: Raving Energy (faster)
tracks.description: There's always someone who is uncomfortably excited. This is for all you border collies hopped up on Adderall. This music is dangerously energetic and may cause paranoia, anxiety, and/or hallucinations.  Not the fun kind of hallucinations, either. These are the kind of hallucinations where ponies with 8 spider-like legs are climbing on your ceiling and walls while singing "Barbie Girl" and criticizing your overly-bland dating profile.

tracks.title: Raw
tracks.description: This low bass guitar piece is dirty ad raw; the strings are forcefully played, and you can hear the vibrations, the squeaks, and the ruggedness, all of which creates a carefree attitude. The drums are barely noticeable. The other bass accompanies the root bass without ever gaining prominence. When the drums stop and the bass plays its final refrain, you can really hear how the music is refreshingly unrefined.

tracks.title: Reaching Out
tracks.description: Rubato.

tracks.title: Ready Aim Fire
tracks.description: An amped up secret agent or pro wrestler theme with a thick wall of sound and a crazy drummer!

tracks.title: Realizer
tracks.description: We would like to interrupt this announcement for a dance break!

tracks.title: Reawakening
tracks.description: Easy love theme; Useful for quiet talks.

tracks.title: Redletter
tracks.description: High-pitched strings play above a low drone, while fuzzy noises and cymbal rolls flow throughout. The high strings crescendo and quickly cut out as if a knife sliced their throats.  A somber melody plays in the final minute, and the noises crescendo and come at you from every angle, symbolic of an attack and a gruesome finale.

tracks.title: Reformat
tracks.description: Sort of 8-bit retro video glitch. Excellent for a lightswitch rave! This piece loops perfectly. The uncompressed download comes in 140bpm and a super-hyped up 170bpm mix!

tracks.title: Reign
tracks.instruments: Piano, Basses, French Horn, Kit, Guitar, Choir
tracks.description: A piece in two parts. Slow piano intro, and then a giant power section at 1 minute 50 seconds in. Written for an animation piece.

tracks.title: Reign Supreme
tracks.instruments: Bassoon, Clarinet, Flute, Bass, Cellos, Violins
tracks.description: Big buildup at the end. So much suspense!

tracks.title: Relaxing Piano Music
tracks.description: You can only title a piece Relaxing Piano Music once in your life, so you better bring it! Piano? You bet! Relaxing? Indeed! Music? Close enough! This 24-minute epic of calm is great for that chilly winter day, or lazy summer day... All the seasons! Wherever you need calm, you can get it here! Peaceful exclamation points? Yes!! All of them! De-stressing while studying for an exam? Go for this one! Doing a retrospective on the life and times of your pet chinchilla? You're welcome! All the calm! ALL THE TIME!!! Key of G. You can make your own mixes with the uncompressed downloads to only include the melodies you want if you like!

tracks.title: Relent
tracks.description: Sadness... so much sadness. Plaintiveness maybe? Anyhoo, very down.

tracks.title: Reminiscing
tracks.description: Simple; mostly pentatonic.

tracks.title: Resignation
tracks.description: Short piece with a very quiet and rich piano part - the bass is barely audible, for low-end support.

tracks.title: RetroFuture Clean
tracks.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

tracks.title: RetroFuture Dirty
tracks.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

tracks.title: RetroFuture Nasty
tracks.description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.

tracks.title: Return of Lazarus
tracks.description: Horrible, horrific, creepy AF... all that stuff. Yuck! :-)

tracks.title: Return of the Mummy
tracks.description: Did you know that people in the 1800s used to make tea out of mummies they dug up in Egypt? Tea. Like the kind you drink. That is because people in the 1800s were dumb. They were so stupid, they thought seaweed was really quite interesting. Today, you would have to be a marine botanist to think seaweed is that exciting. I don't need to mention how "exciting" marine botanists are... Carl! Finding some Caulerpa 20 kilometers outside its published range is no reason to write a paper! And it is certainly no reason to be LATE for your OWN PARTY, CARL!!!

tracks.title: Reunited
tracks.description: Super-sappy well-executed little theme. Really opens up at 38 seconds.

tracks.title: Revival
tracks.description: So you're thinking of doing a revival tour, but you don't have a band to back up your inspirational speech? Good news, good news indeed. This piece starts very thin, and builds a couple of times.

tracks.title: Rhinoceros
tracks.description: Semi-8 bit, sort of 1980's synth pop crazy thing! Super energy; Crazy fun. Perfect for: automobile reviews, actions montages, martial arts clips, or anything with fast edits that needs a good pace!

tracks.title: Right Behind You
tracks.description: Breathy noises make the hairs on the back of your neck stand, while screeching strings and high-pitched noises are distracting and spine-tingling.

tracks.title: Ripples
tracks.description: Flowing like water, this serene piece is perfect for relaxation and meditation. The solitary plucks of the Chinese guzheng reverberate slightly, and maintain a steadiness that would work well for introspective, Asian-themed content. This would also work well for anything depicting snow, winter, or Rural Japan.

tracks.title: Riptide
tracks.description: Straight-up two guitar rock with a few variations. Good background... not the kind of things you'd sit and listen to on its own merit.

tracks.title: Rising
tracks.description: Heavy on the percussion, this piece is dominated by the rising strings in the second minute, which quickly give way to an ethereal alto chorus. The accompaniment rises together before dissipating. Loopable.

tracks.title: Rising Game
tracks.feel: Dark, Driving, Epic, Grooving, Intense, Mysterious
tracks.instruments: Bass, Brass, Percussion, Choir, Guitar, Strings, Pipe Organ
tracks.description: Dark piece in 2 roughly equal main parts. Gets progressively more exciting.

tracks.title: Rising Tide
tracks.description: Let's be fair, if your interview segment was already energetic, you  don't need something like this to fix it. Most people suck at interviews. It isn't their fault. Talking in an entertaining way is really, really,  really hard. That's why this piece exists. Rising Tide is designed to make anyone look good! This piece comes in 2 speeds.

tracks.title: Rising Tide (faster)
tracks.description: Let's be fair, if your interview segment was already energetic, you  don't need something like this to fix it. Most people suck at interviews. It isn't their fault. Talking in an entertaining way is really, really,  really hard. That's why this piece exists. Rising Tide is designed to make anyone look good! This piece comes in 2 speeds.

tracks.title: Rite of Passage
tracks.description: Nice laid-back tribal all percussion piece with overtones of polynesian music.

tracks.title: Rites
tracks.description: Heavy and deep, the chords of this piece resemble Gregorian Chanting with resounding reverb as a harp plucks a few solitary notes. The music evokes an ancient ritual or ceremony, but could also be used for a tragic medieval funeral.

tracks.title: Ritual
tracks.instruments: Alto Flute, Bass Flute, Synths, Percussion
tracks.description: Very very slow piece featuring the alto flute.

tracks.title: River Fire
tracks.description: This piece has 54 beats each minute. At Angkor Wat, a Hindu temple carving has 54 gods in opposition to 54 demons, and in their struggle they create immortality. Mystics (or mathematicians... whatever) in Ancient Greece knew of the prime factorization of this mystic number. 3 by 3 by 3 by 2. What does this all mean? Not much, as it turns out the concept of a "minute" wasn't familiar to the architects at Angkor Wat.

tracks.title: River Flute
tracks.description: I enjoy relaxing background music things. I looked out into the world for this music, and there was a lot of music, but none of it was right. When I want calm - this is the kind of thing I want! Super crazy hit-you-in-the-head calm! I want mega-aggro-calm. The flute in this recording is a standard C flute slowed to half speed. The river is running at normal river speed.

tracks.title: River of Io
tracks.description: I would like to state, for the record, that this is the worst river cruise I've ever taken. The zombie crocodiles were bad enough, but the chase for the stolen artifact statue that was taken by the Ice Monkey Lord was really quite too much. And now I'm missing my left shoe. So why are we up sneaking around UFO landing sites? NONE OF THIS MAKES ANY SENSE!!! You got some clandestine stuff going on? This track will probably work for any sneakiness anywhere.

tracks.title: River Valley Breakdown
tracks.description: Bluegrass country music.

tracks.title: Road to Hell
tracks.description: A slow dark piece featuring a piano, bass duet.  Begins with bass, then immediately piano comes in.  Piece has continuous bass with piano coming in and out.  Finishes with prolonged bass note.

tracks.title: Robo-Western
tracks.description: A smooth glitchy action piece with a guitar sound inspired by Morricone and a setting that is very contemporary.

tracks.title: Robobozo
tracks.description: Deeply satisfying synths play in a slightly dystopian domain. So if you have a film where a future vampire who owns a travelling carnival comes back in time to today with a crazy assemblage of experiences for today's currently not-yet-jaded audiences... that is your piece! Also useful for cat parkour.

tracks.title: Rock Hybrid
tracks.description: Very very clean rock/hip-hop hybrid with some trance elements. EQ'ed dark, vocals should cut right through. Loopable.

tracks.title: Rock on Chicago
tracks.description: Wesley Willis inspired rock music. C major.

tracks.title: Rock Over London
tracks.description: Wesley Willis inspired rock music. A minor.

tracks.title: Rocket
tracks.description: Euro-tech with some highly processed guitar lines and symphonic elements.

tracks.title: Rocket Power
tracks.description: Funky drum machines? Yes, please! Also a killer bass line. This is both big and fun... kind of like the Paul Bunyan Experience... if Paul Bunyan were hip. Unlike most of my tunes, this one has an actual ending! Uncompressed download comes with all the parts to make your own mixes - should this one be insufficient.

tracks.title: Rollin at 5
tracks.description: Acoustic version of "Rolling at 5".

tracks.title: Rollin at 5 - electronic
tracks.description: Electronic only version of "Rolling at 5".

tracks.title: Ropocolypse 2
tracks.description: With a name like "Ropocolypse", it is probably digital and gritty.

tracks.title: Round Drums
tracks.description: A collection of mostly large drums. Useful for action scenes.

tracks.title: Royal Banana
tracks.description: Comically voiced and constructed. Slower (at 90BPM) but it still moves along.

tracks.title: Royal Coupling
tracks.instruments: Flutes, Clarinets, French Horns, Basses, Cellos, Violins, Violas, Tuba, Trombones, Percussion
tracks.description: Light and airy, with a bit of a march going on. Parallel chords and Ravel-like crescendo.

tracks.title: Rumination
tracks.description: After everything is said and done and you have time to look back, this piece unfolds like one's mind coming to terms with situations of gravity.

tracks.title: Run Amok
tracks.instruments: Strings, Tuba, Trumpet, Trombones, Marimba, Clarinet, Bassoon, English Horn, Oboe, Percussion
tracks.description: Super comedy action sequence. You'll know if you need this.

tracks.title: Rynos Theme
tracks.instruments: Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses, Flutes, French Horns, Trombones, Tuba, Percussion, Piano
tracks.description: Starts small, gets big... then smaller, then REALLY big... then small again. Kind of like a turtle. Actually, it is entirely possible that I just kept seeing different turtles. I mean, they all sort of look like turtles; I wasn't tagging them or marking them with chalk or anything. Chalk will probably just wash off in the pond anyway. Oh! Kind of like a puffer fish! Like a musical puffer fish! Perfect.

tracks.title: Salty Ditty
tracks.description: Avast ye maties! All your boat are belong to us! Super chipper piratey-like 8bit tune. I mean, it could be used for non-nautical things, but the audience will probably be all like "Hey! Why is there an 8-bit pirate shanty going on here!?" Perfectly loopable for all your casual seafaring games. Or game reviews. Or actual voyages. Or voyage reviews.

tracks.title: Samba Isobel
tracks.description: Do you eat dinner with no amuse bouche? Then you are not classy enough for this high energy background masterpiece. It exceeds all classiness classifications. It can seem cheery, but that's really just more classiness. The slightly lazy bass player? Classy.

tracks.title: Samba Stings
tracks.description: Various 2-4 second stings based on "Modern Jazz Samba".

tracks.title: Sancho Panza gets a Latte
tracks.description: Acoustic guitar, latin percussion, bass, alto flute, trumpet, and... accordion. Sort of Spanish, sort of French.

tracks.title: Sapphire Isle
tracks.description: Arpeggiation and scales in an unusual chordal setting.

tracks.title: Sardana
tracks.description: Intimate guitar dance piece, probably too rubato to be an actual Sardana, but it didn't sound enough like a Farruca to call it that. "Vaguely Spanish Guitar Music" also seemed wrong.

tracks.title: Satiate
tracks.description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with just the percussion, and just the strings... both of which are quite different from the combined.

tracks.title: Satiate - only percussion
tracks.description: Highly effected percussion piece at a mid tempo. This track was extracted from a larger work, but will lend some motion and reserved immediacy to any scene.

tracks.title: Satiate - only strings
tracks.description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with percussion, which gives it a more immediacy.

tracks.title: Sauropod Spotting
tracks.description: This piece is one of three pieces that was inspired by a trip to a dinosaur-themed roadside attraction that had "dinosaur music". That music was recorded in the early 1990s, and sounds a bit cheesy today, so I tried to update it. This piece is a hybrid of triggered samples and live recordings.

tracks.title: Savannah (Sketch)
tracks.description: This is NOT a complete piece. It is only a sketch developed as a test for a stage production (repeated many times).  If you only need a few seconds, it is fine. Loping feel in 3/4 time.

tracks.title: Sax, Rock, and Roll
tracks.instruments: Kit, Bass, Electric Guitar, Bari Sax, Tenor Sax, Trumpet
tracks.description: Lots of guitars with a sax-y hook.

tracks.title: Scattershot
tracks.description: Fast tempo and loose timing gives this piece some not-quite-in-control speed.

tracks.title: Scheming Weasel (faster version)
tracks.instruments: English Horn, Bassoons, Bass, Glock, Clarinet, Celesta, Triangle, Bass Clarinet
tracks.description: Sort of cartoonish, and yet sort of dark. I couldn't decide the tempo, so I posted a slower and faster version of the piece.

tracks.title: Scheming Weasel (slower version)
tracks.instruments: English Horn, Bassoons, Bass, Glock, Clarinet, Celesta, Triangle, Bass Clarinet
tracks.description: Sort of cartoonish, and yet sort of dark. I couldn't decide the tempo, so I posted a slower and faster version of the piece.

tracks.title: Scissors
tracks.description: Subtle atmospheric sounds and rain-like cymbal elements blend together, creating an aura of intensity and intrigue, suitable for a mysterious or suspenseful production. The sounds build in force just before the end.

tracks.title: SCP-x1x (Gateway to Hell)
tracks.description: Some nice soul-sucking horror music. It looks like an innocent birthday cake. Something mom might buy down at the Jewel’s. It showed up at the holiday party for our Class D personnel last year, but no one knows who brought it. It may be related to SCP-1117. Here’s the problem; you look at that cake too long and it looks back into you. First it fills you with dread, then it fills you with buttercream, ruining your pristine run of ketosis. You were just making progress! Dammit, Cake Demon!

tracks.title: SCP-x2x (Unseen Presence)
tracks.description: Dark horror soundscape. There are places of evil in the world. Dark places. There are places that absorb life with their greasy tendrils of unlight. There are places that screw up everyone's sandwiches. There are places that delay postal packages. There are places that cause internet outages right when you're down to the last 4 players in an online 1 vs 100 Tetris tournament. There are places of evil in the world. Dark places.

tracks.title: SCP-x3x (I am Not OK)
tracks.description: Dark horror soundscape with technological and mechanical overtones.

tracks.title: SCP-x4x (Mind Leech)
tracks.description: Grating Horror Soundscape. Welcome to the Open House! I’m Kathy, your realtor. You’ll probably want to keep your shoes on. On your left is the living room, complete with ornate working fireplace. It’s fueled by the souls of the damned AND it heats the whole house! Mind yourself around the walls, they can get a little grabby if they haven’t been fed yet. Up the stairs and to your right is piece de resistance... the jacuzzi tub! The water filtration system gets out most of the blood. Now, about the attic...

tracks.title: SCP-x5x (Outer Thoughts)
tracks.description: Nice, but creepy music for storytelling. Simple melodies played on that old piano your grandma had in her basement. It was once great, but has since become a spider and dust motel. I'm sure the spiders think it is pretty great. Gotta be loud if you're a piano spider, but rent control totally makes it worth it.

tracks.title: SCP-x6x (Hopes)
tracks.description: Haunting music for storytelling; With a cello. Cello, bassoon, and piano are known to be expert haunters. This piece has no bassoon, but 2 out of 3 does get pretty haunting!

tracks.title: SCP-x7x (6th Floor)
tracks.description: Somewhat urgent music for storytelling. Winding staircase that leads to nowhere... like your liberal arts degree. Melodic enough to hold your interest. Repetitive enough for you to lose interest.

tracks.title: Screen Saver
tracks.description: Blip bloop?  Bloopity BlooBlip! BlooBlip?! Blibbity blib blib blib! Blip bloop. Blippity bloop bloop BLOOP! :-)

tracks.title: Second Coming - no percussion
tracks.description: A loop-based piece, I've gotten a lot of requests for a version of this with no percussion or voice - so here you go. Broad and inspiring.

tracks.title: Secret of Tiki Island
tracks.instruments: Bass, Piano, Percussion, Vibes, Guitar, Vocals, Organ
tracks.description: Co-written with Bryan Teoh while he was on vacation (Thanks Bryan!) this is all the mystery and chill groove you need. So come on you cats and swingers, enjoy yourself a Jet Pilot (served in a pineapple of course) and help unravel the Secret of Tiki Island! Can you save yourself and the island from the Volcano!? No. Of course you can't. It is a freaking VOLCANO. If the pyroclastic flows and lahars don't kill you, the carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide probably will. Uncompressed download comes with 10 different stems so you can mix your own!

tracks.title: Secrets of the Schoolyard
tracks.description: Sort of dark and mysterious, while still being current-sounding and light. Got a mystery in the city? I got your music! Crazy deep bass in lots of parts… careful when mixing this one.

tracks.title: Semi-Funk
tracks.instruments: Kit, Tenor Sax, Trumpet, Bass, Bari Sax
tracks.description: Horn Section with a couple of solos. Nice hook, and the upright bass is beautiful.

tracks.title: Senbazuru
tracks.description: Beautiful warm and calming piece with a Japanese sort of sound. A low end synth provides deep support.

tracks.title: Send for the Horses
tracks.description: Floaty! Ethereal! Useful for dream sequences. Or those montages of sad people standing in the rain.

tracks.title: Serene
tracks.description: A slow, very calm piece featuring English horn, piano, and bass. Center section also has brass ensemble and strings.

tracks.title: Sergio's Magic Dustbin
tracks.instruments: Drums, Tuba, Marimba, Percussion, Clarinets, Flutes, Trumpet, French Horns, Trombones, Glockenspiel, Bassoons, Chimes, Whistles, Cymbals
tracks.description: This piece starts very slow and builds... like Bolero. Unlike Bolero, this piece builds beyond the safety limit and gets crazy. I recommend you check out the piece from 1 minute 48 seconds in. There are several break points you can start from to get to the crazy payoff faster, or use the whole thing!

tracks.title: Serpentine Trek
tracks.instruments: Flute, Clarinet, Bass Clarinet, Alto Flute, Violin, Percussion
tracks.description: Something winding its way somewhere.

tracks.title: Seven March
tracks.description: A piece in 7/8 time with 2-measure phrasing. Very dark and round sounding with randomly placed percussions.

tracks.title: Seven Off
tracks.feel: Unnerving, Eerie, Mystical, Mysterious, Suspenseful, Somber
tracks.description: Lots of strings, a couple of winds carry the interest offset by a glockenspiel. 7-4 time. Slow and unnerving.

tracks.title: Seventh Seal
tracks.description: Simple drone followed by a crescendo leading to silence.

tracks.title: Severe Tire Damage
tracks.description: Ultra-cool downtempo piece with faster driving percussions. Want to look cool? Make this your theme song. Play it loud enough and you can use it for pro-wrestling entrance music! Uncompressed download comes with a bonus 96bpm set.

tracks.title: Shades of Spring
tracks.description: Sort of a minor mid-tempo jazz combo with 2 pianos. Melody is doubled in octaves. Soloist goes outside more than the guy comping... but hey - what are soloists for?

tracks.title: Shadowlands 1 - Horizon
tracks.description: Part one of seven. Sort of an edgy-underwater feel... which isn't common. You can feel the struggle just trying to get the sounds out. Imagine a small rhinoceros at a tea party. The image you have in your head has nothing to do with this piece; But it is quite amusing.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 2 - Bridge
tracks.description: Part two of seven. Very close clusters of tones bring the tension! And that tension wanes and waxes without notice. If you want your audience to be concerned, this is how you do it.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 3 - Machine
tracks.description: Part three of seven. Part pipe organ, part broken pipe organ, this isn't just spooky, it is crazy spooky. It also has a musical theme, which not all of this horror moody stuff has. Consider it the jelly filling in your horror doughnut.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 4 - Breath
tracks.description: Part four of seven. This is the pizza cutter of this series, round and edgy. It has a little bit of melodic complexity, but mostly it just sits around being creepy. Should work well under dialog.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 5 - Antechamber
tracks.description: Part five of seven. Airy, but not in the "I'm outdoors, and everything is great 'airy'" way. More like the "the alien machine that sustains our life is slowly breaking down and poison is beginning to seep from its core" way. Whatever is happening... it isn't fast, and it isn't good.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 6 - The Pit
tracks.description: Part alien cacophony, part organic awfulness, part six of seven. If you set this piece as music you wake up to in the morning, you're going to have a bad, bad day. There will be half remembered monsters from the times of not-asleep, not-awake... whose only jobs are to induce unexpected nausea inside government buildings.

tracks.title: Shadowlands 7 - Codex
tracks.description: Part seven of seven. A real mind bender. This one is all acoustic, and no artificial synths, so it has an organic feel. Not Certified Organic, just normal organic. So, that means it looks better, requires less fertilizer, has fewer pests and a higher yield.

tracks.title: Shamanistic
tracks.instruments: Percussion, Bass Flute, Alto Flute, Xylophone, Synths, Strings
tracks.description: Earthy, yet unearthly. Deep and rich with things amiss.

tracks.title: Shaving Mirror
tracks.description: Hey, yo - welcome to the sic'est grammar podcast on the planet, where your future will have been perfectly continuous. I can't really think up much more in the realm of grammar jokes without going to the "dangling participle". And that's not happening.

tracks.title: Sheep May Safely Graze - BWV 208
tracks.instruments: Small Ensemble - Celesta, Harp, Vibe, Marimba
tracks.description: Bach. Abnormal instrumentation.

tracks.title: Shenyang
tracks.description: When I do music based on folk traditions, I tend to name them after cities. Like this one: Shenyang. It is a little village of 8 million people that I've somehow never heard of. Oh sure, I've heard the name, but I don't associate it with anything specific. Chicago: Hot Dogs. Amsterdam: Offensively tall Dutch. Moscow: "Stop a Douchebag". Shenyang: No clue. How did I miss this city?? You already know if you need this piece, it has a more satisfying low-end than actual real Chinese music, and it should fit in with your modern productions well.

tracks.title: Shiny Tech
tracks.description: Electronica (techo-pop dance). This is a fast and energetic piece polished almost to a fault. Lots of synth, and a happy clave. Think fashion show runway. Works best loud, works also not so loud.

tracks.title: Shiny Tech II
tracks.description: Electronica (techo-pop dance). Much like its predecessor, but with a brand new, less pop main synth line.

tracks.title: Shores of Avalon
tracks.description: Highly processed piano with lots of subtle synths and vocal effects. Grows in intensity after the 3 minute mark, then calms again.

tracks.title: Show Your Moves
tracks.description: Your toe will start tapping to the bump of the bass drum once the music pans through your speakers.  This song is one for a successful accomplishment or the happy ending to a difficult challenge.  The staccato melody resembles a synthesized tremolo violin, while the bass guitar thumps increase  in prominence until they are your heartbeat.

tracks.title: Showdown
tracks.instruments: Flutes, Guitar, Basses, Glock, Marimba, Strings, Brass
tracks.description: Starts unnerving; ends calming.

tracks.title: Sidewalk Shade
tracks.description: Just a nice little jazz piece. A slower version is also available.

tracks.title: Sidewalk Shade - slower
tracks.description: Just a nice little jazz piece. A faster version is also available.

tracks.title: Silly Fun
tracks.description: This is a set of 2 happy bubble-gummy themes for a comic platformer-type video game. Also included in the mp3 file are three different endings - quick, longer, and other.

tracks.title: Silver Blue Light
tracks.description: Sparse in it?s instrumentation, Silver Blue Light is quiet and pensive with atmospheric synthesized chords and guitar.. There isn?t much of a melodic line to this piece until well into the fifth minute. In the third minute the guitar plays a few high notes, and the key changes briefly, which occurs again in the final twenty seconds as well.

tracks.title: Silver Flame
tracks.description: Life is the source of mystical potential. Or it isn't. One of the two. If I had to bet... I would probably ask what those words mean. Even 'life' isn't simple. I don't think I could recognize what the first living thing was. It is like making a soup. Hot water? Not soup. Hot water with salt? Not soup. Add a potato? Still not soup. That's just a potato in hot salt water. At some point it becomes soup. Same with life. Bonus fact: Borscht was never soup. It is borscht.

tracks.title: Simple Duet
tracks.description: Slower, optimistic and simple duet.

tracks.title: Simple Music to Frighten Small Children By
tracks.description: If the title doesn't say it... The sound was accomplished by recording a piano, doubling the recording and pitching one down almost an octave while pitching the other up almost an octave.

tracks.title: Simplex
tracks.description: Thin, dark, moody piece that accelerates to the end. Remarkably metered and free at the same time. Guitar is all half muted.

tracks.title: Sincerely
tracks.description: Talk wistfully about the past.  Talk hopefully about the future.  Talk about your hopes and fears.  Talk about your neighborhood watch lady.  Talk about your chill tracks!

tracks.title: Sinfonia No. 3 in D Major - BWV 789
tracks.description: Bach's 3-part invention with a hip beat and bass. The notes are all Bach's, but are not all in the correct order.

tracks.title: Sinfonia Number 5
tracks.description: J. S. Bach's 3-part invention that I hacked together for music for a "stuffy aristocratic dinner party". Of all the Sinfonias, I think this works the best for that.

tracks.title: Sing Along with Jim
tracks.instruments: Trumpet, Glock, Marimba, Kit, Tenor Sax
tracks.description: Peppy yet easy children's music designed to be easy to make up a song to.

tracks.title: Skye Cuillin
tracks.instruments: Harp, Whistle, Fiddle, Synths, Strings, Choir
tracks.description: New age and Celtic with super round synths and lots of delay.

tracks.title: Sleep and Then
tracks.description: Winds descending, strings ascending. Slow, nice.

tracks.title: Slow Burn
tracks.description: Super nice progressive rock/blues piece with 3 sections.

tracks.title: Slow Heat
tracks.description: Very simple polyrhythms and polymelodies.

tracks.title: Slow Jam
tracks.description: Well, this is interesting... Smooth sine bass contrasted with a lovely excited drum machine and then... the magic! Genre bending magic! You're a cool kid right? This is for you. You're welcome. Think 'trap' meets 'R&B' meets 'shoegaze' meets some other genre that is SO COOL there isn't even a name for it yet. Download comes with a not-quite-so-slow version that is not quite so slow.

tracks.title: Slow Ska Game Loop
tracks.description: Two very different synths bracket the highs and lows of this piece. Loopable for things that require looping.

tracks.title: Smash (Sketch)
tracks.description: This is NOT a complete piece. It is only a sketch developed as a test for a stage production (repeated many times).  If you only need a few seconds, it is fine. This piece has a harsh ting-y electric piano on top.

tracks.title: Smoking Gun
tracks.instruments: Bass guitar, Guitar, Choir, Flute, Strings
tracks.description: Gritty Western feel with a touch of suspense.

tracks.title: Smooth Lovin
tracks.description: This one got turned up to 11. I started producing this as a parody... then I really started liking it, so I guess it is a pastiche now? Oh, man... I wish there was an allowance for pastiche in copyright like there is for parody.

tracks.title: Smooth Move
tracks.description: A Simple Bass Groove with High Hat and Snare behind it. The repeated bass line is good for dancing.

tracks.title: Smoother Move
tracks.description: Super rubato piano solo.

tracks.title: Snare Bounce Polka
tracks.description: Swing.

tracks.title: Sneak 'n Get Caught
tracks.description: Low strings / glass harmonica. Wind/String/Percussion diminished chord build with crescendo and sting on the end. (written for Darker Projects' Falcon Banner Episode 4)

tracks.title: Sneaky
tracks.description: Ascending and descending chromatic scales gives this piece an air of mischief; perfectly suited for a cartoon. It has moments of tenuous fluidity, rapid motion, and a touch of suspense, making it perfect for the classic scene where the hero is sneaking past the sleeping giant.

tracks.title: Sneaky Adventure
tracks.description: Tight pizz string section, joined by a lone bassoon on the recapitulation.

tracks.title: Sneaky Snitch
tracks.description: An oboe and a snare drum dance a tantalizing number with the whimsical plucks of a string quartet. The staccato nature of the music suggests walking on tiptoes, while the nasal notes of the oboe flits about almost imperceptibly. In the final minute, the string quartet plays a simple rhythm, before the oboe and snare drum crescendo to the finale.

tracks.title: Soaring
tracks.description: While not an epic hour-long relaxation juggernaut, Soaring is an excellent relaxation workhorse with just enough mystical qualities to keep it from being truly peaceful.  Imagine a calm monkey hanging out at a remote monastery who, from time to time, will touch a tree - causing the tree to age a decade in a matter of seconds. I mean... still pretty calm, but something isn't right about that.

tracks.title: Sock Hop
tracks.description: 1950's era simple rock with tremolo lead guitar and vibraphone. Almost surf music.

tracks.title: Some Amount of Evil
tracks.instruments: Clarinets, Bass Clarinet, Xylophone, Strings, Piano
tracks.description: Starts at a fast pace, and slows.

tracks.title: Somewhere Sunny
tracks.description: Simple, clean guitar duet.

tracks.title: Somewhere Sunny (ver 2)
tracks.description: This is a longer version of the very popular "Somewhere Sunny". Simple, clean guitar duet.

tracks.title: Son of a Rocket
tracks.description: Deeply bassy club-style chords.

tracks.title: Sonata 17
tracks.description: A short piece for small orchestra. The flutes play off the bassoon well. The B section includes a pleasant string theme. This piece culminates in a nice, easy ending.

tracks.title: Song of the Volga Boatmen
tracks.description: Yo, Heave Ho! The classic theme of difficult drudgery. Based on a Russian folk song.

tracks.title: Soporific
tracks.description: A laid-back chill, and chilling piece.

tracks.title: Southern Gothic
tracks.description:
Are you cool? Cool like a vampire planking in a graveyard in Alabama? 
Planking is uncool... so, you gotta be really, REALLY cool to pull off this vibe.
Stomp and clap along to the cooperating banjos!

tracks.title: Sovereign
tracks.description: Very very good new age piano solo in a minor. You might think 6 minutes is a bit long, but it isn't. Played on a darkly voiced piano. This piece should in no way be offered for free.

tracks.title: Sovereign Quarter
tracks.description: A re-recording of an older piece of mine on a new sample set of a Steinway Model D. This one is tuned to Quarter Comma Meantone (and not standard Equal Temperament).  In this piece, it gives an unerringly warm feel, as the notes that would be least in tune in this are never used.

tracks.title: Space 1990
tracks.description: Do you have enough 1990's space music in your collection? Probably not. If you're unclear what 1990s pace music is, just take a listen. A slightly different mix is also available at a faster tempo.

tracks.title: Space 1990-B
tracks.description: This is about as fast as you can reasonably push such a piece. Smooth and warm.

tracks.title: Space Fighter Loop
tracks.description: Written as a background loop for a space fighting video game.

tracks.title: Space Jazz
tracks.description: While working on a video game, the script called for "Space Jazz". I don't know if that is a thing, but this is what I made. Sounds like Space Jazz to me!

tracks.title: Space X-plorers
tracks.description: Background padding with an open wondrous feel.

tracks.title: Spacial Harvest
tracks.description: Deep unsettling piece with no repeated themes. Fat, rounded bass drone with very high pitched interest on top.

tracks.title: Spacial Winds
tracks.description: Clear bowed-bell theme over a sweeping dark digital pad.

tracks.title: Spazzmatica Polka
tracks.description: Boisterous and nearly obnoxious, this piece will lodge itself in your brain and make you think you?re trapped in an arcade. The polka rhythm is quick and the melody is spastic. Right into the second minute the rhythm drops out and introduces a crazed, comedic melody that continues throughout until the abrupt end.

tracks.title: Special Spotlight
tracks.description: So you're producing an interview segment! Problem is most people suck at being interviewed. Like... almost everyone. What do you do? You could send the non-media professional to an improv class, you could do 5 pre-interview coachings, or you could schedule a 3-day "pre-interview" at an all-inclusive beach resort in hopes that you will "share a moment" and uncover some goddamn humanity in your interview subject. Or. You could just put some interesting music behind the segment. If your crap interview is longer than this piece Do NOT loop this music - fire your editor.

tracks.title: Spellbound
tracks.description: Reverbs, reverbs, reverbs! You want reverbs in you music, you got reverbs right here! Room reverbs, plate reverbs, even some spring reverbs! It is amazing! It is incredible! How can there be so much reverb?! So... why... You get a very hollow spooky thin feeling with the reverbs. This started out as an attempt to understand Witch House music. Pretty sure I still don't understand it.

tracks.title: Spider Eyes
tracks.description: Spider Eyes is an eerie soundscape created with distant high strings, dissonant non-percussive piano textures, and alternately tuned bells.  This piece features much sustain and space.

tracks.title: Spider's Web
tracks.description: Harpsichord in tritones with a bass pedal.

tracks.title: Spirit of the Girl
tracks.description: There are 54 beads on a Buddhist prayer mala. These are used for counting recitations and chants. There are 54 beats per minute in this song. Coincidence? Sure is. What, you're going through an entire mala cycle in a minute? That's crazy talk! Studies have shown the optimal number of mantras in a single set is somewhere between 15 and 20 anyway... so don't waste your money on the 54 or 108 bead versions. You'll be a lot better doing more sets of less reps. And don't forget leg day.

tracks.title: Split In Synapse
tracks.description: A short piece that mixes the symphony with frenzied electronica elements and a dance beat. The horns are blasting and discordant, the synthesizer is manic, the effects disorienting, and the final cresecendo push is loud and forceful.

tracks.title: Spring Thaw
tracks.description: Simple melody. Something feels amiss here, but in a sort of pleasing way

tracks.title: Spy Glass
tracks.instruments: Piano, Bass, Drums, Vibes, Saxes, Trumpet, Flute
tracks.description: The year is... I have no idea. Timeless. Could be now, could be in the 1950s. Super cool jazz for your hardcore detectives! Also useful for beat poets! Also useful for ennui or boredom! Well, interesting sorts of boredom.

tracks.title: Spy Groove
tracks.instruments: Kit, Organ, Bass, Cellos, Conga, Bass, EP, Violin
tracks.description: Aggressive drum kit sound with warmth added by a B3 organ and conga. Modulation in the final repeat.

tracks.title: Stages of Grief
tracks.description: That sort of "I'm kind of 'ok', but I'm still standing out in the rain feel". Pretty depressing for being in a major key.

tracks.title: Starry
tracks.description: C major with a minor IV chord.

tracks.title: Starting Out Waltz Allegretto
tracks.description: This is more for practicing dance than anything else. It never changes, it never gets interesting. This is important if you don't want to trip over your feet while drilling a dance step.

tracks.title: Starting Out Waltz Vivace
tracks.description: This is more for practicing dance than anything else. It never changes, it never gets interesting. This is important if you don't want to trip over your feet while drilling a dance step.

tracks.title: Static Motion
tracks.description: Sharp subtle percussive clicks accompany with otherworldly drone.

tracks.title: Stay the Course
tracks.description: A low rumble marks the seconds. Out of nowhere comes nothing! Just a continuous ominous force, never seen. You can see the ominous force if you sprinkle some iron filing around.

tracks.title: Stealth Groover
tracks.description: The constancy of the bass melts into your consciousness, as the syncopation of the high-pitched piano and electric guitar keep the groove flowing. Subtle synthesizer arrangements change the flow of the song and keep it interesting, while the rhythm section is playful and experimental. This is perfect for a scene where the spy learns a new skill or performs an act of guile, or as the background to a low-key, tech-oriented game.

tracks.title: Steel and Seething
tracks.description: Nice build-up and release. See also: Medusa

tracks.title: Steel Rods
tracks.description: Smashing on a dumpster while pulling off some imitative counterpoint. Is it a fugue? Nah.

tracks.title: Still Pickin
tracks.description: Good old fashioned pickin and stompin!

tracks.title: Stoic Morning
tracks.description: Impromptu. Bright and cheery, but never bubbly. It does change up into minor for a bit.

tracks.title: StompDance
tracks.description: Starts slowly, and accelerates, ending on a quick note.

tracks.title: Stoneworld Battle
tracks.instruments: Percussion, Tubas, Trombones, French Horns, Baritones, Strings
tracks.description: Giant movie battle sound kicks in at 2:00 with the finale starting at 2:50.

tracks.title: Stormfront
tracks.description: Intense and reserved, this unrelenting piece of drumming will be well at home in the soundtrack of your summer blockbuster. Super long for splicing.

tracks.title: Street Party
tracks.instruments: Organ, Bass, Drums, Percussion, Trumpet, Trombone, Sax, Horns
tracks.description: This is my impression of a tv show street party scene scored by a composer from the 90s. #TexasSharpshooterFallacy

tracks.title: Strength of the Titans
tracks.instruments: Hurdy Gurdy, Percussion, French Horns, Trombones, Tubas, Cellos, Basses
tracks.description: Oh, this is a big one. Short, but big. There's nothing wrong with either of those things.

tracks.title: String Impromptu Number 1
tracks.description: Soaring and delicate piece for full string orchestra.

tracks.title: Stringed Disco
tracks.instruments: Kit, Bass, Strings, EP, Wah Guitar
tracks.description: Wah guitar, strings, octave jumping bass, and THE disco beat.

tracks.title: Study And Relax
tracks.description: Like a worn out record with a mis-punched spindle hole. Thanks, izope! :-)

tracks.title: Style Funk
tracks.instruments: Kit, Bass, Wah Guitar, Electric Guitar, Horn Section
tracks.description: Cool, cool funk. Some horns for punctuation.

tracks.title: Suave Standpipe
tracks.instruments: Bass, Accordion, Drums, EP, Guitar, Horns, Organ, Synth, Sax, Vibes
tracks.description: You know what's cool? A standpipe in the winter. I imagine this one with a hip mustache and a plaid beret. Enough of the imagery, this is a little downtempo chill piece with lush horn punctuation. Suitable for: walks in the rain, time-lapse videos, sad cooking shows.

tracks.title: Sugar Plum Breakdown
tracks.description: Just the final part of Tchaikovsky's piece with giant percussion and synths.

tracks.title: Sugar Plum Dark Mix
tracks.description: Tchaikovsky's dance  from the Nutcracker with lots of percussion and extra choirs.

tracks.title: Summer Day
tracks.description: Soothing piece with an interesting harmonic left-turn. You got a savage beast? This is just the ticket.

tracks.title: Summon the Rawk
tracks.description: Double kick drums, aggressive bass... perfect for: entrance music for pro-wrestlers, annoying the neighbors, playing "air drums", long walks on the beach.

tracks.title: Sunday Dub
tracks.description: This was written for a sneaky-yet-cool scene. The kind where our main character is trailing a subject to find out where they get the amazing cheese they serve at their restaurant. There's a bunch of bits where the paranoid restauranteur turns around unexpectedly and Private Detective Alice Winterbottom has to duck behind dumpsters, or spin around casually pretending to be on a phone call, or hide behind a watermelon at the fruit stand.

tracks.title: Sunflower Dance Party
tracks.description: As much fun as you can have with a cowbell! Lots and lots of cowbell.  I wrote this one when I was particularly depressed, and it fixed it. I didn't want it to end, so I kept modulating it; that's why it is longer than most.

tracks.title: Sunset at Glengorm
tracks.description: Processed piano is featured, leaving a deep uncertain texture. Tempo is highly variable.

tracks.title: Sunshine
tracks.description: A bright piece with piano and rhythm guitar throughout.  Kit and Bass in the background.  Main melody carried by Piano.

tracks.title: Sunshine (version 2)
tracks.description: Slightly longer, slightly slower version of "Sunshine"

tracks.title: Suonatore di Liuto
tracks.description: Simple little background lute piece.

tracks.title: Super Circus
tracks.description: Circus-type march.

tracks.title: Super Friendly
tracks.description: Starts easy, builds, and releases easy again. Sort of like a happy triumph. Eucatastrophe, even.

tracks.title: Super Polka
tracks.instruments: Kit, Trumpet, Clarinet, Bass, Electric Guitar
tracks.description: Super smashing trumpets, and a crazy clarinet! Also guitars and such. Not your oom-pah kind of polka. This is all-out dance.

tracks.title: Super Power Cool Dude
tracks.description: This piece was built almost entirely with arpeggiators. What does that mean for you? Probably nothing. But holy man! Does this sound like it is from 1983! So, pop a tape of "Flashdance" in your VCR... and then spend like 8 minutes rewinding it... because, apparently your cousin couldn't be bothered to do that. Seriously, Sally! You did the same thing when I lent you "Smokey and the Bandit II", and I didn't say anything because you had a hard week, but still managed to make the Jell-o Salad with the grapes for the family reunion... which was nice. Anyway, I'll probably just get you one of those $20 tape rewinders they have at Radio Shack for your birthday. I also enrolled you in the Battery of the Month Club. You're welcome.

tracks.title: Supernatural
tracks.description: A quick little piece to bring out supernatural elements.

tracks.title: Supernatural Radio A
tracks.description: If you're looking for that late 40s/early 50s sci-fi or supernatural radio drama - this is your piece. This was rendered on a hammond, using only the drawbars that would make it over the radio (no bass).

tracks.title: Surf Inspector
tracks.description: Bouncy piece, usable in spy setting.  Stays similar throughout, easily looped, if necessary.

tracks.title: Surf Shimmy
