tracks.description: I gotta admit, I've never been to a clambake, only ever fish boils... which are similar, except for clambakes usually involve mollusks and giant sea-bugs, and fish boils involve fish. Also, clambakes are more steaming and fish boils are more boiling. You're more likely to see Green Bay Packers jerseys at fish boils, and more likely to see New England Patriots jerseys at clambakes. This music is west-coast, though... The more I think about it - the less useful this descriptive paragraph becomes. Uncompressed download comes with a couple mild variations, including "Psychedelic".

tracks.title: Suvaco do Cristo
tracks.description: Named for a region in Rio, this Brazilian-style carnival piece has a deep dark thickness to it.

tracks.title: Sweeter Vermouth
tracks.instruments: Tenor Sax, Alto Sax, Trumpets, Vibes, Trombones, Kit
tracks.description: The jaunty bass line keeps this short piece moving at a solid pace, while the vibraphone and saxophones play the swinging melody, until the bright, thump of an ending. Use this piece as a slick transition between scenes or for the background to a short scene of drinking, gambling, or dancing.

tracks.title: Swimmey Texture
tracks.description: Highly processed piano and synths that provide a deep, contemplative texture.

tracks.title: Symbiosis
tracks.description: Quiet solo piano in 3 parts with additional percussion bit adding in more and more to the end. My normal "feels" that are used to classify pieces are largely inadequate for this piece, as are the genres. In other words... I have no idea what this is.

tracks.title: Symmetry
tracks.description: This piece has a good beat and you can dance to it... assuming you are a dark, lurking horror with a betentacled face and an urge to consume life forces.

tracks.title: Tabuk
tracks.description: An epic plodding middle-eastern sounding piece. Grab your camels!

tracks.title: Tafi Maradi
tracks.description: Percussion beats and shakers instantly make your feet tap, involving you in the tribal experience of ritual kinship. Three sets of call-and-response chanting slide into the forefront of the beat, interspersed with rapid djembe solos to the ending when the dust finally settles.

tracks.title: Tafi Maradi no voice
tracks.description: Percussion beats and shakers instantly make your feet tap, involving you in the tribal experience of ritual kinship. Three sets of call-and-response chanting slide into the forefront of the beat, interspersed with rapid djembe solos to the ending when the dust finally settles.

tracks.title: Take a Chance
tracks.instruments: French Horn, Trombone, Strings, Xylophone, Percussion, Flute, Clarinet
tracks.description: An out of control epic ride of adventure!

tracks.title: Take Me Out to the Ballgame
tracks.description: Ballpark organ playing the peppy classic.

tracks.title: Take the Lead
tracks.description: This is a rough and hard-hitting piece, best used as background music to a stressful, strained scene, or tense and suspenseful content. Heavy distorted guitars begin the song, and at 0:41 the soaring synth leads play the melody while the powerful drums kick in.  A high-pitched pulsating synth effect carries the last seventeen seconds to the final punch.

tracks.title: Takeover of the 8-bit Synths
tracks.description: This... uhh... hmm... let's call it 'experimental' piece starts out with vanilla guitar and rock drums, and gets progressively crazier as the 8-bit synths take over the piece. Maximum anarchy starts around the 3-minute point.

tracks.title: Tango de Manzana
tracks.instruments: Piano, Bass, Drums, Flute, Violin, Accordion
tracks.description: A tango in 2 chords.

tracks.title: Taps v2
tracks.description: Solo trumpet version of the 1862 military ceremonial piece.

tracks.title: Tea Roots
tracks.instruments: Bass, Kit, Erhu, Organ, Guitar, Piano, Horns
tracks.description: Almost straight-up reggae, but with a chinese folk violin in it.

tracks.title: Tech Live
tracks.description: Interview-Mania! This piece does nothing and goes nowhere. Perfect for an energetic backdrop to your review or interview segments!

tracks.title: Tectonic
tracks.description: Sister piece to Earth Prelude. Battle sequence.

tracks.title: Teddy Bear Waltz
tracks.instruments: Flute, Glock, Clarinet, Cellos, Violas, Basses
tracks.description: Technically speaking, I think this one is in 6/8 time... in which case, the tempo it 75. If it was notated in 3/4 time, the tempo would be 225 bpm. This piece took almost exactly one year to go from initial idea to produced piece. What was I doing for a whole year!? I mean... it doesn't exactly sound that difficult.

tracks.title: Teller of the Tales
tracks.description: Simple subtle plucked duet of ancient-inspired origins.

tracks.title: Temple of the Manes
tracks.description: An ancient-feeling modal piece.

tracks.title: Tempting Secrets
tracks.description: Starts with a big hit, and then a steady string drone with a beautiful flute line on top. Choirs kick in 2/3 of the way to bring up the mood.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act One
tracks.instruments: Organ, Percussion, Glock, Voice, clarinet, strings, tuba
tracks.description: This peculiar piece does have a story. If anyone would like to animate it, you'll have to bring your own script. Moderately large changes every minute or so. Accelerando at the end.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Three
tracks.description: Metallic and generally unpleasant... yet I like this piece quite a bit. It gives the impression of a giant mechanical automaton.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Two
tracks.description: A fast deep unyielding sort of waltz-like-thing.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Intermission
tracks.description: Grooves for a bit, then changes up pretty hard with giant percussion.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Mermaid
tracks.feel: Eerie, Intense, Mysterious, Mystical, Relaxed, Suspenseful, Unnerving
tracks.instruments: harps, voice, exotic organ, waterphone, percussion, glass harmonica
tracks.description: Is she a mer-maid, or is she an illusion! Her enchanting voice will entice, and she is 100% alive! Keep your wits about you, gentlemen - you don't want to be dragged to an unfortunate end.  Very heavy on bass.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Prelude
tracks.description: Originally released in a special collection as "Delayed Due to Dissonance", this piece is not part of a larger arc.

tracks.title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Snake Lady
tracks.description: One of the more sultry sideshow acts in the Tenebrous Brothers Carnival, The Snake Lady is a crowd favorite that most never forget, even if they don't remember exactly what happened during the show.

tracks.title: Texture for Violincello and Pianoforte No. 2
tracks.description: An interesting jumble of cello and some piano fused together to create an eerie and intense piece the likes of which no one has ever heard of...until now.

tracks.title: That Zen Moment
tracks.description: I picked up a round metal tongue drum from a local music store a while back, and thought the chords were beautiful. End of story! Enjoy the zen. :-)

tracks.title: That's a Wrap
tracks.description: Sparse music compatible for voice-over. This piece is related to the Rock piece "Welcome to the Show"

tracks.title: Thatched Villagers
tracks.description: Solid in pace, The Thatched Roof Villagers moves with percussion and a number of flutes and pipes struggling for dominance. The real joy of the piece is halfway through when the tinny dulcimer plays the melody and is then joined by the flutes in melody and harmony. The music is jovial and inviting. Loopable.

tracks.title: Thaxted (Holst)
tracks.description: Written by Gustav Holst, 1921; Arranged by Kevin MacLeod 2006. Originally published in a hymnbook - this piece took readily to the WWII retrospective type of arrangement.

tracks.title: The Bandit
tracks.description: Short Theme in two tempos for your bad guy.

tracks.title: The Britons
tracks.description: Tavern music like from the olden days.

tracks.title: The Builder
tracks.instruments: Strings, Bass, Cello, Viola, Violin, Brass, Tuba, Trombone, Trumpet, Woodwinds, Bassoon, English Horn, Oboe, Percussion, Marimba
tracks.description: Comedic, free-wheeling fun!

tracks.title: The Cannery
tracks.description: A giant rousing mechanized heavy piano and heavy percussion piece, mildly reminiscent of Gershiwn or Scott - in 2 small sections.

tracks.title: The Chamber
tracks.feel: Dark, Eerie, Epic, Mystical, Suspenseful, Unnerving
tracks.instruments: Harps, Bass Clarinet, Bassoon, Low Brass, Strings, Choir, Percussion
tracks.description: Delicate start with a lush ending.

tracks.title: The Chase
tracks.description: Light and fast. For... well - chase sequences.

tracks.title: The Complex
tracks.feel: Action, Aggressive, Dark, Driving, Epic, Intense, Mysterious
tracks.description: Mechanistic, electronic and organic. This piece gets very big around 1:46. (The preview is more 'boomy' than the download.)

tracks.title: The Curtain Rises
tracks.instruments: violins, french horn, tympani, brass, percussion
tracks.description: A short bit of fanfare, like the kind that opens movies. Trillerific!

tracks.title: The Descent
tracks.instruments: French Horns, Trombones, Tuba, Violins, Percussion, Trumpet
tracks.description: Driving piece without an overpowering melody. Should fit nicely into a lot of scenes.

tracks.title: The Dread
tracks.description: Background horror music. Electronic. Slow, rumbly, and whiny Moderately unnerving.

tracks.title: The Entertainer
tracks.description: Scott Joplin composition.

tracks.title: The Escalation
tracks.description: One really long build. Generally gets faster, fuller and more exciting. Like "Bolero" but for suspense.

tracks.title: The Forest and the Trees
tracks.description: A peaceful exploration of the interplay between woodwinds weaving through a melody, underscored by soft brass chords. The music evokes scenes of nature, acceptance, and quietude.

tracks.title: The Hive
tracks.description: Cymbals and synthesizers evoke swarming insects, as whirring and clicking noises abound with heavy reverb.

tracks.title: The House of Leaves
tracks.description: A simple harp refrain plays a child?s melody, but is torn apart by discordant screeching noises, thumps, growls, and mechanical noises.

tracks.title: The Ice Giants
tracks.instruments: French Horns, Trombones, Tubas, Euphonium, Trumpets, Cimbasso

tracks.title: The Lift
tracks.description: A little trance-y and a dance-y, this piece takes a while to develop (like most EDM things these days). The full width of the piece is realized around 1:40. Not so much a drop and a gentle trip down a hill, really - but still satisfying! That note at the end? Surprisingly difficult to do that... I know you're thinking - Hey! That just sounds like noise! Well, yes and no. But it is worth it!

tracks.title: The Machine Thinks
tracks.description: 100% electronic creepiness. Change from round and bleeping to harsh bleeping about 2 minutes in.

tracks.title: The North
tracks.description: Loopable small composition reminiscent of North American traditional music.

tracks.title: The Other Side of the Door
tracks.description: A quick and off-color melody on the harp transports you to a mystical eerie world, while a flute plays a sweet melody, and pizzicato strings create a playful undertone. Quite a bit happens in this piece musically, it can be used to complement scenes of mischief, an eerie scene, or a world of magic and intrigue.

tracks.title: The Parting
tracks.instruments: Oboe, Flute, Strings, Trombones, Horn, Tuba
tracks.description: I wrote this one December 27th, 2009 mainly for fun. It is a sweeping quiet piece until the past bit where is opens up a bit.  At 2:06, there is an oddly supported line with a 2+ octave gap between the melody and the supporting bass. At 2:28, the gap is filled triumphantly... It ends with a hollow dominant in 5 octaves, followed by a lush resolution.

tracks.title: The Path of the Goblin King
tracks.instruments: Strings, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Celesta, Tympani
tracks.description: This is sort of "Spooky Light". It is dark yet playful in a sense. Good for fairy tales or light tension building. It has several small arcs in it - but loops back to the begging.

tracks.title: The Path of the Goblin King v2
tracks.instruments: Strings, Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Celesta, Tympani
tracks.description: Slightly faster version of the other similarly named piece, this one has an extra sense of urgency, but still retains the mystery and wonder bits.

tracks.title: The Pyre
tracks.description: Vaguely medieval overtones. The opening section repeats in the second half with violins added.

tracks.title: The Reveal
tracks.instruments: Orchestral - Cello, Horn, English Horn, Clarinet, Contratuba
tracks.description: Starts with cellos, adds horn, clarinet, English horn, contra-tuba - to a final sustained chord. Slow. Thin yet satisfying.

tracks.title: The Rule
tracks.instruments: Trumpets, French Horns, Trombones, Tuba, Bells, Tympani
tracks.description: I sort of regal opening brass fanfare. It is meant to join at the end with another piece of music... which has not been written yet. This works as a stand-alone opening for most anything.

tracks.title: The Second Coming
tracks.description: A sound track piece with Kit and Trombones/French Horns throughout.  This piece includes sections from a public domain (librivox) reading of "The Second Coming."

tracks.title: The Second Coming Instrumental
tracks.description: A sound track piece with Kit and Trombones/French Horns throughout.

tracks.title: The Show Must Be Go
tracks.instruments: Bass, Guitar, Diddley Bow, Clarinet, Trumpet, Vibraphone, Horns, Kit, Percussion
tracks.description: Sort of inspired by the 1930s, and sort of inspired by all-out weird. Definitely recommend taking a listen to this piece. Make sure you get to the 1 minute mark... fun times trumpet playing await! I personally enjoy how the clarinet play tries to follow the trumpet player - doesn't work out so well.

tracks.title: The Sky of our Ancestors
tracks.description: We reflect, we dream, we are born. We gather together, we smile, we eat potato salads. We remember, we invent, muddle mint for our mojitos. We greet, we listen, we appreciate NetFlix. We collect coins and stamps... for some reason. We mix up the names of our children with the names of our pets. We x-ray baggage... with X-RAYS! Those things are like 200keV! Each! Do you know what that does to people!? Hint: Not good things.

tracks.title: The Small
tracks.description: Simple polyrhythms in a very small piece. Get it? Small!? Epsilon!?? Yeah... no worries. The fifth of a series.

tracks.title: The Snow Queen
tracks.instruments: Strings, Bassoon, Bass Clarinet, Flute, Celesta, Tympani
tracks.description: Sort of exciting and sort of spooky in that fairy tale sort of way. This is one of my favorite pieces of late. Good interplay of instruments. You can listen to this one over and over. Handy, because it does loop back to the beginning. Major build starting at 1:50 or so.

tracks.title: The Voices
tracks.description: Almost comforting pad, were it not for the inhuman voice-like punctuations.

tracks.title: The Way Out
tracks.description: Understated intensity with a hair of creepiness.

tracks.title: The Whip
tracks.description: The shorter theme written for the opening of The Whip Podcast. Starts off quick with a short drum roll, then continues with guitar.  Guitar used throughout, ends with a fade out using Kit.  Bass in the background only.

tracks.title: The Whip (Extended Version)
tracks.description: The extended version of the show theme written for The Whip Podcast.  Aggressive, hip, theme.  Slow fade out at the end.  This version can be looped easier than the shorter version.

tracks.title: Theme for Harold (var. 1)
tracks.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the laziest and slowest of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

tracks.title: Theme for Harold (var. 2)
tracks.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the mid-tempo version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

tracks.title: Theme for Harold (var. 3)
tracks.description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the fastest "Boss Level" version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.

tracks.title: There is Romance
tracks.description: Slow and poignant, this piece is excellent for depicting childhood love, the swelling love of adolescence, or the tender caresses of old age. The simple, elegant melody is exceptionally suitable to weddings, faith services, or as a theme to a story of lasting love.

tracks.title: There It Is
tracks.description: Very quick and jovial, this brass heavy piece has a guitar riff that sticks in the brain, but ends suddenly. Useful for a quick theme introduction, transition, or for a fast and exciting commercial.

tracks.title: Thief in the Night
tracks.description: Laid-back, grooving, and cool. Did I mention cool? You need a cool piece. That is a statement you NEED a cool piece. Lucky for you, this IS a cool piece. Super clean production will allow this piece to fit into most things. I'd personally use this piece for a super badass character.

tracks.title: Thinking Music
tracks.description: Comedic "hard thinking" music. Chances are you won't need the entire piece if you are making a film. I made it so you can cut it up into different sounding sections of various seriousness. If you're using it for a video game, everything flows together well, or you could loop sections that work best.

tracks.title: Thinking of You
tracks.description: Nice piece for a narrative voice-over of good times past, present or future.

tracks.title: Thinking Out Loud
tracks.description: Piano looped digital electronica hybrid. I started this piece in 2

tracks.title: This House
tracks.instruments: Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses. Piano, Harp, Celesta, French Horn, Waterphone
tracks.description: Delightfully creepy, this piece is really difficult to listen to without squirming a bit. I blame the violins... as we all should. Perfect for any scene where something just ain't right!

tracks.title: Thunder Dreams
tracks.description: This is more of a chordal soundscape than a drone. There is a little bit of hope here and there, but it is tempered with a deep sadness. Probably useful after a loss. Beautiful, horrible.

tracks.title: Thunderbird
tracks.description: Wikipedia describes the Thunderbird as "a supernatural bird of power and strength". It will also ask you to disambiguate it from the automobile made by Ford from 1955 to 2005. I'm sure it was a nice car. I've never owned one. But there were a lot of them! The late 70's Thunderbirds are particularly horrifying... They had those headlight covers that flipped up... because that was a good idea at some point. But this piece! Oh! This piece! Atmosphere like you wouldn't believe! The flute is just so earthy! The organic drones are also beautiful. The whole thing is beautiful. Kind of like you went to an alien day spa in another dimension where days last for years, but you still never get all wrinkly when you're in the bubbly warm waters. mmmm... bubbly warm waters... with the slight possibility of a serial killer.

tracks.title: Thunderhead
tracks.description: Native American drumming. The branch rattle is reminiscent of thunder. Tempo picks up about halfway through.

tracks.title: Tiki Bar Mixer
tracks.description: How to make Tiki Drinks: Add rum. Add fruit juice. Add other rum. Add different fruit juice. Add another rum. Add some other juice thing. Top with crushed ice. Garnish with umbrella, flowers, pineapple, watermelon, small plastic dinosaurs, and sugar cane. Light on fire.

tracks.title: Tikopia
tracks.description: The feel of this percussion pieces switches from straight to swing several times, but always has a round wooden sound to it.

tracks.title: Time Passes
tracks.description: Bittersweet and somewhat dark; ends brightly on an open major chord.

tracks.title: Tiny Fugue
tracks.description: A very short fugal theme. (3-part imitative counterpoint)

tracks.title: To the Ends
tracks.instruments: Bassoon, Bass Clarinet, Oboe, Clarinet, Trombones, Violins, Basses,
tracks.description: Horns used in the background.  Main melodies carried by clarinet and strings.  Starts off bright, ends darker.

tracks.title: Toccata and Fugue in D Minor
tracks.description: J. S. Bach's most famous organ piece. BWV 565. (Beckerath German baroque pipe organ)

tracks.title: Too Cool
tracks.description: You know when you watch a vampire movie and then you walk out into the real world, but you're still sort of in the fictional world because it looked like the real world... and that's where you are now. I call this Persistence of Fiction, and it feels awesome! Capture some fiction by playing this track while walking to the bus... er the Vampire Bus! or waiting in line at the Vampire DMV or sorting Vampire Direct Mail Ads or doing some Vampire Macrame.

tracks.title: Touching Moments Five - Circle
tracks.description: A simple tour through every major key in order. Arpeggiated with some connecting melodic notes.

tracks.title: Touching Moments Four - Melody
tracks.description: More melodic than most of the pieces presented here - can be distracting, or can be just what you're looking for. Famous from the Sad Fairy Dress-up game.

tracks.title: Touching Moments One - Pulse
tracks.description: Open and airy. A classic "touching moment" style. Performance imperfections are exaggerated to give a more "choked up" feel.

tracks.title: Touching Moments Three - Deeper
tracks.description: A more 'gutsy' piece that explores more of the keyboard, and provides a more grounded and open feel.

tracks.title: Touching Moments Two - Higher
tracks.description: Only notes from the very highest registers of the piano are used in this. It can cut through ambient noise and still provide a presence.

tracks.title: Touching Story
tracks.description: Very very slow and changeable.

tracks.title: Townie Loop
tracks.description: Welcome to the town! If you have anything to sell, just put it in the box. The general store sells seeds. There is a Mountain Totem in the mountains. You can have a drink at the Iridium Bar. I need to tend to my giant melons now. That is not a euphemism. Bye!

tracks.title: Tranquility
tracks.description: A calming meditative piece rendered on 4 iPhones using the Balls, Bloom, Bebot, and Ocarina applications.

tracks.title: Tranquility Base
tracks.description: Super chill, meditative, and massively long drone. The preview is cut to three minutes, but the entire download is 18 minutes, and more than 42 meg. Please be patient.

tracks.title: Transition One
tracks.instruments: Orchestral - Flute, Clarinet, Bass Clarinet, Bass, Cello, Viola, Violin, Glock, Harp
tracks.description: Small calm transition; descending wind ensemble blending to ascending string ensemble.

tracks.title: Trepidation
tracks.description: Background horror music. Solo piano; low and loud.

tracks.title: Trio for Piano Violin and Viola
tracks.description: An unfinished trio in 2 main parts.

tracks.title: Trio for Piano, Cello, and Clarinet
tracks.description: More contemplative than outright depressing. Tempo is highly variable, so don't count on it if you have to synch to something. I didn't know there was a tradition of writing for this instrumentation. It works very well.

tracks.title: Trips It
tracks.description: A driving electronic piece.  Kit is dominant throughout the piece.  Choir has brief moments about 55 secs in, and re-emerging for a heavier role towards the end half of the piece.

tracks.title: Trouble
tracks.description: Diminished chords, tremolo You'll recognize them.

tracks.title: Trouble with Tribals
tracks.description: Another exciting guerrilla warfare planning meeting, and Parker didn't bring the coffee. I'm starting to get annoyed with Parker more and more these days. Sure, the new "cape cod style" curtains look great in the mud blinds, but I'm not into the satin obelisk in the middle of our jungle huts.

tracks.title: Truth in the Stones
tracks.description: New age music. You know what is cool about New Age music? Low ambitions. It wants to do a simple thing, and then does it. No crazy counterpoint. No complicated harmonic structures. Just a simple simple thing. Like if Tetris was all those long blocks. Man, that would be great.

tracks.title: Truth of the Legend
tracks.description: Solo voice along with a small choir and giant percussion section. Ends in a sort of ethereal mode.

tracks.title: Twisted
tracks.description: A modern take on a 1970’s rock style.

tracks.title: Twisting
tracks.description: Let's talk about why so much film music sounds like this. The construction allows any part to be muted and otherwise sculpted around the dialog without the loss of a theme or motive energy. There isn't really a theme to lose. You can't hum this one easily. There is a lot of variation, but it is all in a very well defined range, and doesn't get too crazy.

tracks.title: Two Finger Johnny
tracks.description: Remember the old Casio and Yamaha "auto accompaniment" keyboards? This is a super-simple and freakishly-delightful terrible piece of music.

tracks.title: Two Together
tracks.description: Sparkly open voicings.

tracks.title: Tyrant
tracks.description: Crank it up, ladies and gentlemen!  Come on! Let's go! You know HOW TO CRANK! Let's go clockwise! Like... clockwise from the top - not the bottom. Grab it from the top. Either hand. It doesn't matter. Now CRANK IT! Crank it. ...like how a clock moves. The other way. If you take the part farthest from  you and move it to the right... Counter-widdershins? You know what, it doesn't really need to be cranked.

tracks.title: Ujangong Mix
tracks.description: An epic clash of genre that feigns coherence. Based on the Public Domain 1904 recording of "Ujangong (Mask Dance)" from New Guinea. But with a swing bass and slicing techno chunk in 3/4 time.

tracks.title: Ultra Polka
tracks.description: I tried to do an EDM piece using one of my new accordions... turns out, accordion just doesn't have the fast attack needed to do fast electronic things. The melody and chords were written for a diatonic button box, but I was never able to get the live recording to work. No worries! I just turned this monster up to 11. The uncompressed download comes with a faster and slower version.

tracks.title: Ultralounge
tracks.instruments: Piano, Bass, Synths, Percussion, Drums, Congas
tracks.description: You hip? You really hip? Oh, yeah you are! This piece comes from the coolest hippest parts of solar system... from a 1960s pad on the moon. Oh yeah. Dig it, man... dig it. The uncompressed download also comes with an even more chill mix.

tracks.title: Umbrella Pants
tracks.description: If naming tracks is so easy, you try it! Possibly sneaking, possibly comedic dialog, possibly comedic dialog while sneaking... 1,

tracks.title: Unanswered Questions
tracks.description: The solid beat and dark melody reverberate, giving the simplicity of this single-instrument piece the feeling of mounting tension and unease. Useful for a documentary showing pain, poverty, or imprisonment.

tracks.title: Undaunted
tracks.description: Big big drums pushing a big cinematic feel.

tracks.title: Unease
tracks.description: Background horror music. Solo midrange piano.

tracks.title: Unholy Knight
tracks.instruments: Organ, Percussion, Choir, Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses, Trumpets, Trombones, Tuba, French Horns, Cimbasso, Clarinets, Flutes, Oboes
tracks.description: Oh geez, there's lots of notes in this one. The end of this piece is just woodwinds by themselves, and they are super cool. So often the percussion just takes over these pieces, even though there are some beautiful parts that get attention directed away from them.

tracks.title: Unity
tracks.description: Big driving piano and drums piece for action goodness!

tracks.title: Universal
tracks.description: Floating and grounding, this piece has a lot of bass guts but still a lot of reach on the high end. Perfect for retrospectives, automobile time lapses, drunken frat parties (black and white), and studying montages.

tracks.title: Unlight
tracks.feel: Aggressive, Dark, Eerie, Epic, Intense, Unnerving
tracks.instruments: Basses, Cellos, Violins, Trombone, French Horn, Trumpets, Flutes, Clarinets, Percussion
tracks.description: This piece is actively painful. It is ugly and nasty and dirty - about as much as you can be using exactly one orchestra. Seriously, there are occasional bits where there are notes - but mostly, it is just... uhh...

tracks.title: Unnatural Situation
tracks.description: Piano with a tape delay and lots of dark colour in the background.

tracks.title: Unpromised
tracks.description: Thin piece with surprising chordal structures in the second A section.

tracks.title: Unseen Horrors
tracks.instruments: Strings, Basses, Cellos, Violins, Brass, Percussion
tracks.description: I originally wrote this as a piece for theramin, but I think it works better without.

tracks.title: Unwritten Return
tracks.description: Dreamy and edgy; Not a combination you often find, and yet - here it is. The ambiguous and slippery nature of the piece are a wonderful thing. Perfect for scoring a character where the audience is unsure of them. Could be good? Could be evil? WE DON'T KNOW!

tracks.title: Up on a Housetop
tracks.instruments: Piano, Tuba, Kit, Bari Sax, Tenor Saxes
tracks.description: Super-bouncy holiday sing-along.

tracks.title: Upbeat Forever
tracks.description: Ska! Ska! Ska! At least, I hope it gives that impression. Works pretty well for a lively background to most anything! This was written for an improv comedy group... so they would have something reasonable to sing to - if an audience member suggests it.

tracks.title: Urban Gauntlet
tracks.description: Action-y intense like percussion based piece. Need to defuse a bomb while riding in a pedi-cab? This should work well for that. Or anything where tension needs to be maintained.

tracks.title: Vadodora
tracks.description: Quite a hip little tune. Also available without the melody.

tracks.title: Vadodora Chill Mix
tracks.description: Quite a hip little tune. Also available witha cutting melody.

tracks.title: Valse Gymnopedie
tracks.description: This is Gymnopedie #1 from Erik Satie (1888), but it has a beat and you can dance to it.

tracks.title: Vanes
tracks.description: A disturbingly sweet melody on an electric piano is accompanied with a slow and steady beat. Synth sounds undulate in the background, fighting for prominence. They ultimately melt away, leaving the piano melody to play one last despair-filled refrain.

tracks.title: Vanishing
tracks.instruments: Prepared Piano, Bass Clarinet, Cello, Clarinet, English Horn, Tuba, Trombones, French Horns, Oboe, Synth, Violin, Flutes
tracks.description: Several distinct moods are found in this piece. They start at 0:00, 1:23, 2:31, and 3:10. They do all flow into each other, but can be sliced apart pretty easily. Some are quite beautiful, so stick with this piece. Excellent piece for filmmakers!

tracks.title: Variation on Egmont
tracks.description: Kind of techno, with a mix in of themes from Beethoven's overture as played on piano.

tracks.title: Vegas Glitz
tracks.description: This sounds happier than anything with parallel chords should.

tracks.title: Verano Sensual
tracks.description: This one was designed to be played at low volumes under people doing things like talking or fixing broken PS4s. Spicy, spicy broken PS4s. Mmmm....

tracks.title: Very Low Note
tracks.description: Just a very low note (a C) to be used as a bed for any very unnerving and dark scene.

tracks.title: Vibe Ace
tracks.description: Starts more synthy ends more organic.

tracks.title: Vibing Over Venus
tracks.instruments: Vibraphone, Bass, Drum kit, Percussion, Strings, Piano
tracks.description: It is relaxation hour here on Radio Kilimanjaro, the only all-live music, 24-hour frequency on your radio dial! Tonight is going to kick off with Alice Goodworth on her vibraphone, playing along to the famous Radio Kilimanjaro Automaton Ensemble. She calls this piece "Vibing Over Venus"... and you all know why! (It is because she plays vibes... [which is a musical instrument.])

tracks.title: Vicious
tracks.description: Bit of swing in your rap? Sure! Why not! I like swing... but NOT TOO MUCH! Just here and there... you know, to alleviate the monotony. Sort of like that one teacher you had in Social Studies that unexpectedly did something cool - like play a game - but only twice a year... and they were both in the first month, so all you ended up with was 8 months of continual disappointment. Screw you, Mr. Meuller! I still don't care about checks and balances!

tracks.title: Video Dungeon Boss
tracks.description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Crawl is similar but slower.

tracks.title: Video Dungeon Crawl
tracks.description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Boss is similar but faster.

tracks.title: Village Consort
tracks.description: Picture a pixellated medieval village... cause that's what this is. It is the kind of music we think they played back in the day. It is not historically. But I'm okay with that, because we also didn't have lich-kings, lich-mages, lich-illithids, lich-warriors, or lich-archers. We did have lichens, though... I like lichens!

tracks.title: Village Dawn
tracks.description: Light piece in 5/8 time with a Lydian subsection.

tracks.title: Villainous Treachery
tracks.description: The melody for this piece is in the bass keys, while the high notes play a headache-splitting constant rhythm. At the one-minute mark the high-pitched notes drop several octaves to play a crunched staccato before returning to the previous theme. The last thirty seconds feature drawn out chords, and the tempo slows dramatically, ending with frustrated trills in both registers, signaling the demise of the villain.

tracks.title: Villainous Treachery - Distressed
tracks.description: The melody for this piece is in the bass keys, while the high notes play a headache-splitting constant rhythm. At the one-minute mark the high-pitched notes drop several octaves to play a crunched staccato before returning to the previous theme. The last thirty seconds feature drawn out chords, and the tempo slows dramatically, ending with frustrated trills in both registers, signaling the demise of the villain.

tracks.title: Vintage Education
tracks.description: Intended to imitate the style of the 1970's educational programming.

tracks.title: Virtutes Instrumenti
tracks.description: Based on 11th century sacred music, this piece can set you way way back in time almost instantly. Several faster and slower sections are available during this piece.

tracks.title: Virtutes Vocis
tracks.description: Based on 11th century sacred music, this pieces carries melodies only, and no words.

tracks.title: Vision of Persistence
tracks.description: Rhythmically driven simple piece, high and sweet.

tracks.title: Vivacity
tracks.description: Happy, peppy, vibraphone piece. Sounds like the late 1950's or early 1960's.

tracks.title: Voice Over Under
tracks.description: This is a piece of music classified as "GNDN". Goes Nowhere. Does Nothing. It sort of sits there and just repeats mild variants. There isn't even an ending.  Yet, this was all on purpose. This piece was designed for keeping energy in news reports or review segments where there is a lot of talking. There is no end so it is easy to loop to any length. There will come a time in your editing career where you will need this piece. Best to download it now.

tracks.title: Volatile Reaction
tracks.instruments: Brass, Trombone, French Horn, Tuba, Contrabass Bassoon, Bassoon, Bass Clarinet, Clarinet, Flute, Piccolo, Violin, Viola, Cello, Bass, Percussion
tracks.description: 7/4 time, blasting brass, pounding percussion. Suitable for fights, evil, or a calm day at the park... in hell.

tracks.title: Voltaic
tracks.description: You know that sound that was big in 80s dance music with that sort of galloping doo-do-do-DAH-do-do-doo-do-do-DAH thing? This has a thing like that, but in really, really complex drum sound. You need to wait until 16 seconds in to hear what the doo-do-do-DAH-do-do-doo-do-do-DAH sounds like. I know it can be difficult reading KRN (Kevin's Rhythmic Notation). A-do-do-dooo-a-da-da-daaah is all I want to say to you.

tracks.title: Vortex
tracks.description: Blatting brass ensemble. Uneven phrasing.

tracks.title: Voxel Revolution
tracks.description: Is it chiptunes? Nope. Is it 80s? Nope. We had to wait 40 years for this stupid fusion! 40 Years!!! It is really happy, though. Like when an underdog video game character is doing a level-up montage, or that song that plays in a 13 year old's head when they get an extra mozzarella stick.

tracks.title: Vulcan
tracks.description: A mystical piece for Flutes, Bells, and Percussion.  Disjointed melodic flute in counterpoint with lower fluttery flutes, plodding  percussion, and shimmering bells. Same texture throughout piece.

tracks.title: Wagner Bridal Chorus
tracks.description: The classic "here come the bride" piece written by Wagner for the opera Lohengrin. This is about as traditional a performance as you can get.

tracks.title: Wagner Bridal Chorus - piano
tracks.description: A newer piano variation on Wagner's Bridal Chorus. It leaves out some of the less familiar middle section, and changes up a few chords while retaining the melody.

tracks.title: Wagon Wheel
tracks.description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.

tracks.title: Wagon Wheel - Electronic
tracks.description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.

tracks.title: Wah Game Loop
tracks.description: Just a simple funk/rock piece for looping anonymously in the background of things. Organ seems a bit nasal. hmm...

tracks.title: Walking Along
tracks.description: Written as a laid-back background for a film where a calming feel was needed.

tracks.title: Wallpaper
tracks.description: Very very clean mix that is non-offensive on almost all fronts. Good spectral distribution - nice lows and highs. 2 catchy synth lines sort of fight for attention, leaving you to ignore them both after a while.

tracks.title: Waltz (Tschikovsky Op. 40)
tracks.description: Opus 40; Number 9. Written 1878. Recorded 2005.

tracks.title: Waltz of the Carnies
tracks.description: Creepy off-putting circus music. Also features some honking horns later in the piece.

tracks.title: Waltz of Treachery
tracks.description: Light but dim. Nice for a 'classy' villain with a plan.

tracks.title: Waltz Primordial
tracks.description: Featuring the genuine Nordic Metal talents of Alexander Nakarada.

tracks.title: Water Droplets on the River
tracks.description: 6/8 piece meant to be reminiscent of nice memories from long ago.

tracks.title: Water Lily
tracks.description: Simple and elegant.

tracks.title: Water Prelude
tracks.description: Smooth background music... Float-y feeling.

tracks.title: Waunobe March
tracks.instruments: Trumpets, Trombones, Tuba, Flutes, Clarinets, Piccolo, Snares, Bass Drum, Alto Sax, Tenor Sax, Bari Sax
tracks.description: A simple march as played by a semi-competent 23-piece ensemble.

tracks.title: We Got Trouble
tracks.description: Super action, but still a bit restrained. Quite a long cue with a few changes on the inside.

tracks.title: We Wish you a Merry Christmas
tracks.instruments: Oboe, Celesta - Violin, Clarinet - Piano, Strings, Brass, Glock, Kit
tracks.description: Starts out slowly and accelerates as it builds.

tracks.title: Weight of Responsibility
tracks.instruments: Orchestral - Horn, Trombone, Tuba, Trumpet, Cello, Viola
tracks.description: Brass ensemble with a slight bit of strings. Deliberate chorale sounding, free conducted. Evocative of a sense of nobility and weariness. Loopable.

tracks.title: Welcome to HorrorLand
tracks.description: Welcome to HorrorLand! Please keep all arms, legs, and eyestalks inside the vehicle at all times. All exits are clearly marked. There are no exits. Do not attempt to leave HorrorLand. This will end badly for everyone. Please note: it will end badly if you do not attempt to leave as well. So, it is really up to you. Feel free to split up your group and explore. That is always a great idea!

tracks.title: Welcome to the Show
tracks.description: A one-chord wonder designed to open a show. It has a long lead out for fading. Modulation about halfway through.

tracks.title: Wepa
tracks.description: Need an upbeat vaguely urban-sounding piece to run under your video outro? That's why I made this! You're welcome.

tracks.title: Werq
tracks.description: This is destined to be a podcast theme. If you're starting a podcast, get this now before someone else does. You know it's perfect. Plus is is easy to type the title in your credits. I'm looking out for you, podcaster! All hail the Podfather, Adam Curry. Yes, that Adam Curry. Yes, he really did invent podcasts.

tracks.title: Western Streets
tracks.instruments: Snare, Tenor drum, Tympani, Chimes, Gong
tracks.description: An all percussion tension-sustaining piece... More chaotic than symmetric, but enough repeated themes to keep it cohesive.

tracks.title: Wet Riffs
tracks.description: Solo bass with a looping pedal. Very very slow. Super nice. Starts with the highs, and builds interest in the bass.

tracks.title: What Child is This
tracks.description: Very very high and thin.

tracks.title: What Is Love
tracks.description: What is love? Apparently, it is an odd mix of 1980's synthy love songs and modern trap beats. I don't think there is anything like this out there... which may be a fine thing - or I've just invented a genre. Crooner-Synth Trap-Pop.

tracks.title: What You Want
tracks.description: Super aggressive distorted piece with vocal effects.

tracks.title: What You Want (version 2)
tracks.description: Same as the other version, but with no intelligible vocals.

tracks.title: When The Wind Blows
tracks.description: Several wind instruments play lilting melodies that are slow and meander through the piece, sometimes bordering on being slightly out of tune. The calm music has an edge of solemnity about it. The ever-present acoustic guitar is methodical and resembles a pulse ? it exists but is forgotten, except when the guitar draws out the length of a note.

tracks.title: Whimsy Groove
tracks.description: Lighter and more fun small drum ensemble. Tumba, Conga, Quinto, Bells, and lots of Marimba.

tracks.title: Whiskey on the Mississippi
tracks.description: With a jumping bass and off-beat syncopation, this is straight from Memphis? Beale Street. The Hammond organ and electric guitar play together as longtime friends, while the melody changes hands from guitar to organ to electric piano.

tracks.title: White
tracks.description: Easy flowing with highly differentiated right and left hand parts.

tracks.title: White Lotus
tracks.description: Interesting new age sort of piece, that meets you halfway in the beginning with a lush, but brittle metallic soundscape. As it progresses - the metals fall away, and you're left with a bed of pure sine waves, and a piano tuned exactly to go along with them.

tracks.title: Who Likes to Party
tracks.description: There are 70s bits, 80s bits, 90s bits.... all soft of mashed up in a salad-mash-soup-like thing.  Super crisp dance mix.

tracks.title: Wholesome
tracks.description: Nothing but good, wholesome instruments here. None of those dirty electric guitars, synths, drum kits, harps, sackbuts, or pipe organs. Heh, organs.

tracks.title: Willow and the Light
tracks.description: Think dark overgrown forest with overtones of magic in it. This one can loop perfectly - if you cut it right.

tracks.title: Wind of the Rainforest
tracks.description: Would you believe this is computer-generated? I would believe that. I would totally believe that.

tracks.title: Windswept
tracks.description: A relaxed guitar and strings piece for the denouement of a story or exposition of the scenic outdoors. The guitar is peaceful as the strings gently build in prominence. The tempo is regular overall, but slows down in key moments to build a sense of tranquility.

tracks.title: Winner Winner!
tracks.instruments: Violins, Violas, Cellos, Basses, Percussion, Xylophone, Choir, Glock
tracks.description: Hard to get more fun than this. Seriously, it is insane fun.

tracks.title: Winter Chimes
tracks.description: Interesting piano solo with a repeated pedal in the right hand. Counterpoint on the final repeat.

tracks.title: Winter Reflections
tracks.description: A calming piece rendered on 3 iPhones using the Bloom, Bebot, and Balls applications.

tracks.title: Wish Background
tracks.instruments: Piano, Strings, Bells, Celesta, Brass Ensemble
tracks.description: A sort of holiday backdrop. Variations on a traditional holiday piece. Modulations every 5 minutes or so. VERY LARGE FILE.

tracks.title: Wisps of Whorls
tracks.description: This is about as calming as you can get and still have some sound.

tracks.title: Witch Hunt
tracks.instruments: Percussion, Low Brass, Violins, Winds, French Horn
tracks.description: Several feel changes from strictly percussive to full orchestral. Ends on a piercing high.

tracks.title: With a Creation
tracks.description: An experimental piece, designed to emulate a keyboardist with her robot.  The piano player likes to play with the EP in this piece.  Take a listen to get the full effect.  EP used heavily throughout the entire piece.  Build at 1:02, percussion picks up with heavy, fast beats.

tracks.title: With Regards
tracks.description: Music for a vigil. Very chill, almost hymn-like.

tracks.title: With the Sea
tracks.description: Darker, slow and contemplative impromptu.

tracks.title: Wizardtorium
tracks.description: Very airy and eerie. Based off of a feel of Holst's 'Neptune'.

tracks.title: Work is Work
tracks.description: Light and cheery. Appropriate for nearly any application.

tracks.title: World Vice
tracks.description: Piece in three parts (appx 1 minute each), all up-tempo. Written for a juggling competition.

tracks.title: Wounded
tracks.description: It is rain outside the window on the day of your husband's funeral. maybe not exactly that... but there's death involved somehow.

tracks.title: Wretched Destroyer
tracks.instruments: Basses, CellosBassoons, English Horn, Percussion, Pipe Organ, Basses, Violins, Violas, Percussion
tracks.description: Have you ever heard a 4 bassoon ensemble before? Not likely. While bassoonists may create temporary pair-bonds, they are never found in groups of 3 or more. Much digital trickery was involved in this piece to make them appear as though they were all in the same room at the same time. Tuba players, on the other hand exhibit extreme flocking behaviour, and have even been spotted in mass migrations.

tracks.title: Yallahs
tracks.description: Dark tones and a wah guitar in a modern-mix classic-sounding reggae piece.

tracks.title: Your Call
tracks.description: A little funky; a little disco; this one will keep you grooving on hold for many hours on a loop! Your Call is very important to us! Also excellent for elevators or anywhere light music can be heard.

tracks.title: Zanzibar
tracks.description: Energetic without being aggressive. This one has a nice flow and interesting changes.

tracks.title: Zap Beat
tracks.description: Perfectly loopable for background applications that need a little bit of drive that doesn't annoy.

tracks.title: Zazie
tracks.instruments: Clav, Bass, Percussion, Voice, Mouth Trumpet
tracks.description: Hey there, swingers and swingees! Grab your berets and cigarettes for this trip to a hip Euro-Space-Age Lounge Music Adventure! Vous ne devriez pas amener un canard à combattre les Belges. Il est important d'avoir un mot de passe fort. Vous souvenez-vous de "Le Manège enchanté"? Parce que je ne me souviens pas de ça.

tracks.title: ZigZag
tracks.description: A little aggressive, a little chill, a little groovy, a little cool. Not entirely appropriate for all occasions, but in the right context - it may be just what you need! This is the "Goth 7th-Grader" of the music world. The instrument with the sharp chord hits is the mighty Mellotron, which is a pre-sampler sort of analog keyboard attached to a bunch of tape players. I cheated. This one is digital.

tracks.title: Zombie Chase
tracks.feel: Driving, Action, Unnerving, Dark, Mysterious, Suspenseful
tracks.description: Aggressive, but smooth action sequence; earthy and powerful, using the same piano theme as Zombie Hoodoo.

tracks.title: Zombie Hoodoo
tracks.description: Simple piano line with dark atmospherics in the background. It says "Zombie", but it is useful for any number of creepy motifs. (This piece is related to Zombie Chase).
